quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: The Cowardly Lion was much pleased to hear that the Wicked Witch had been melted by a bucket of water, and Dorothy at once unlocked the gate of his prison and set him free. They went in together to the castle, where Dorothy's first act was to call all the Winkies together and tell them that they were no longer slaves.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: There was great rejoicing among the yellow Winkies, for they had been made to work hard during many years for the Wicked Witch, who had always treated them with great cruelty. They kept this day as a holiday, then and ever after, and spent the time in feasting and dancing.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "If our friends, the Scarecrow and the Tin Woodman, were only with us," said the Lion, "I should be quite happy."
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "Don't you suppose we could rescue them?" asked the girl anxiously.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: So they called the yellow Winkies and asked them if they would help to rescue their friends, and the Winkies said that they would be delighted to do all in their power for Dorothy, who had set them free from bondage. So she chose a number of the Winkies who looked as if they knew the most, and they all started away. They traveled that day and part of the next until they came to the rocky plain where the Tin Woodman lay, all battered and bent. His axe was near him, but the blade was rusted and the handle broken off short.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "Oh, yes. Some of us are very good tinsmiths," they told her.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "Then bring them to me," she said. And when the tinsmiths came, bringing with them all their tools in baskets, she inquired, "Can you straighten out those dents in the Tin Woodman, and bend him back into shape again, and solder him together where he is broken?"
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: The tinsmiths looked the Woodman over carefully and then answered that they thought they could mend him so he would be as good as ever. So they set to work in one of the big yellow rooms of the castle and worked for three days and four nights, hammering and twisting and bending and soldering and polishing and pounding at the legs and body and head of the Tin Woodman, until at last he was straightened out into his old form, and his joints worked as well as ever. To be sure, there were several patches on him, but the tinsmiths did a good job, and as the Woodman was not a vain man he did not mind the patches at all.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: When, at last, he walked into Dorothy's room and thanked her for rescuing him, he was so pleased that he wept tears of joy, and Dorothy had to wipe every tear carefully from his face with her apron, so his joints would not be rusted. At the same time her own tears fell thick and fast at the joy of meeting her old friend again, and these tears did not need to be wiped away. As for the Lion, he wiped his eyes so often with the tip of his tail that it became quite wet, and he was obliged to go out into the courtyard and hold it in the sun till it dried.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "If we only had the Scarecrow with us again," said the Tin Woodman, when Dorothy had finished telling him everything that had happened, "I should be quite happy."
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: So she called the Winkies to help her, and they walked all that day and part of the next until they came to the tall tree in the branches of which the Winged Monkeys had tossed the Scarecrow's clothes.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: It was a very tall tree, and the trunk was so smooth that no one could climb it; but the Woodman said at once, "I'll chop it down, and then we can get the Scarecrow's clothes."
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: Now while the tinsmiths had been at work mending the Woodman himself, another of the Winkies, who was a goldsmith, had made an axe-handle of solid gold and fitted it to the Woodman's axe, instead of the old broken handle. Others polished the blade until all the rust was removed and it glistened like burnished silver.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: As soon as he had spoken, the Tin Woodman began to chop, and in a short time the tree fell over with a crash, whereupon the Scarecrow's clothes fell out of the branches and rolled off on the ground.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: Dorothy picked them up and had the Winkies carry them back to the castle, where they were stuffed with nice, clean straw; and behold! here was the Scarecrow, as good as ever, thanking them over and over again for saving him.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: Now that they were reunited, Dorothy and her friends spent a few happy days at the Yellow Castle, where they found everything they needed to make them comfortable.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: But one day the girl thought of Aunt Em, and said, "We must go back to Oz, and claim his promise."
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "Yes," said the Woodman, "at last I shall get my heart."
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "And I shall get my brains," added the Scarecrow joyfully.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "And I shall get my courage," said the Lion thoughtfully.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "And I shall get back to Kansas," cried Dorothy, clapping her hands. "Oh, let us start for the Emerald City tomorrow!"
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: This they decided to do. The next day they called the Winkies together and bade them good-bye. The Winkies were sorry to have them go, and they had grown so fond of the Tin Woodman that they begged him to stay and rule over them and the Yellow Land of the West. Finding they were determined to go, the Winkies gave Toto and the Lion each a golden collar; and to Dorothy they presented a beautiful bracelet studded with diamonds; and to the Scarecrow they gave a gold-headed walking stick, to keep him from stumbling; and to the Tin Woodman they offered a silver oil-can, inlaid with gold and set with precious jewels.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: Every one of the travelers made the Winkies a pretty speech in return, and all shook hands with them until their arms ached.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: Dorothy went to the Witch's cupboard to fill her basket with food for the journey, and there she saw the Golden Cap. She tried it on her own head and found that it fitted her exactly. She did not know anything about the charm of the Golden Cap, but she saw that it was pretty, so she made up her mind to wear it and carry her sunbonnet in the basket.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: Then, being prepared for the journey, they all started for the Emerald City; and the Winkies gave them three cheers and many good wishes to carry with them.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: The next morning the sun was behind a cloud, but they started on, as if they were quite sure which way they were going.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "If we walk far enough," said Dorothy, "I am sure we shall sometime come to some place."
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: But day by day passed away, and they still saw nothing before them but the scarlet fields. The Scarecrow began to grumble a bit.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "We have surely lost our way," he said, "and unless we find it again in time to reach the Emerald City, I shall never get my brains."
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "Nor I my heart," declared the Tin Woodman. "It seems to me I can scarcely wait till I get to Oz, and you must admit this is a very long journey."
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "You see," said the Cowardly Lion, with a whimper, "I haven't the courage to keep tramping forever, without getting anywhere at all."
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: Then Dorothy lost heart. She sat down on the grass and looked at her companions, and they sat down and looked at her, and Toto found that for the first time in his life he was too tired to chase a butterfly that flew past his head. So he put out his tongue and panted and looked at Dorothy as if to ask what they should do next.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "Suppose we call the field mice," she suggested. "They could probably tell us the way to the Emerald City."
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "To be sure they could," cried the Scarecrow. "Why didn't we think of that before?"
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "We have lost our way," said Dorothy. "Can you tell us where the Emerald City is?"
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "Certainly," answered the Queen; "but it is a great way off, for you have had it at your backs all this time." Then she noticed Dorothy's Golden Cap, and said, "Why don't you use the charm of the Cap, and call the Winged Monkeys to you? They will carry you to the City of Oz in less than an hour."
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "I didn't know there was a charm," answered Dorothy, in surprise. "What is it?"
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "It is written inside the Golden Cap," replied the Queen of the Mice. "But if you are going to call the Winged Monkeys we must run away, for they are full of mischief and think it great fun to plague us."
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "Won't they hurt me?" asked the girl anxiously.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "Oh, no. They must obey the wearer of the Cap. Good-bye!" And she scampered out of sight, with all the mice hurrying after her.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: Dorothy looked inside the Golden Cap and saw some words written upon the lining. These, she thought, must be the charm, so she read the directions carefully and put the Cap upon her head.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "Ep-pe, pep-pe, kak-ke!" she said, standing on her left foot.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "What did you say?" asked the Scarecrow, who did not know what she was doing.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "Hil-lo, hol-lo, hel-lo!" Dorothy went on, standing this time on her right foot.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "Ziz-zy, zuz-zy, zik!" said Dorothy, who was now standing on both feet. This ended the saying of the charm, and they heard a great chattering and flapping of wings, as the band of Winged Monkeys flew up to them.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: The King bowed low before Dorothy, and asked, "What is your command?"
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "We wish to go to the Emerald City," said the child, "and we have lost our way."
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "We will carry you," replied the King, and no sooner had he spoken than two of the Monkeys caught Dorothy in their arms and flew away with her. Others took the Scarecrow and the Woodman and the Lion, and one little Monkey seized Toto and flew after them, although the dog tried hard to bite him.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: The Scarecrow and the Tin Woodman were rather frightened at first, for they remembered how badly the Winged Monkeys had treated them before; but they saw that no harm was intended, so they rode through the air quite cheerfully, and had a fine time looking at the pretty gardens and woods far below them.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: Dorothy found herself riding easily between two of the biggest Monkeys, one of them the King himself. They had made a chair of their hands and were careful not to hurt her.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "Why do you have to obey the charm of the Golden Cap?" she asked.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "That is a long story," answered the King, with a winged laugh; "but as we have a long journey before us, I will pass the time by telling you about it, if you wish."
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "Once," began the leader, "we were a free people, living happily in the great forest, flying from tree to tree, eating nuts and fruit, and doing just as we pleased without calling anybody master. Perhaps some of us were rather too full of mischief at times, flying down to pull the tails of the animals that had no wings, chasing birds, and throwing nuts at the people who walked in the forest. But we were careless and happy and full of fun, and enjoyed every minute of the day. This was many years ago, long before Oz came out of the clouds to rule over this land.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "My grandfather was at that time the King of the Winged Monkeys which lived in the forest near Gayelette's palace, and the old fellow loved a joke better than a good dinner. One day, just before the wedding, my grandfather was flying out with his band when he saw Quelala walking beside the river. He was dressed in a rich costume of pink silk and purple velvet, and my grandfather thought he would see what he could do. At his word the band flew down and seized Quelala, carried him in their arms until they were over the middle of the river, and then dropped him into the water.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "And what became of them?" asked Dorothy, who had been greatly interested in the story.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "Quelala being the first owner of the Golden Cap," replied the Monkey, "he was the first to lay his wishes upon us. As his bride could not bear the sight of us, he called us all to him in the forest after he had married her and ordered us always to keep where she could never again set eyes on a Winged Monkey, which we were glad to do, for we were all afraid of her.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "This was all we ever had to do until the Golden Cap fell into the hands of the Wicked Witch of the West, who made us enslave the Winkies, and afterward drive Oz himself out of the Land of the West. Now the Golden Cap is yours, and three times you have the right to lay your wishes upon us."
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: As the Monkey King finished his story Dorothy looked down and saw the green, shining walls of the Emerald City before them. She wondered at the rapid flight of the Monkeys, but was glad the journey was over. The strange creatures set the travelers down carefully before the gate of the City, the King bowed low to Dorothy, and then flew swiftly away, followed by all his band.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "That was a good ride," said the little girl.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "Yes, and a quick way out of our troubles," replied the Lion. "How lucky it was you brought away that wonderful Cap!"
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: The four travelers walked up to the great gate of Emerald City and rang the bell. After ringing several times, it was opened by the same Guardian of the Gates they had met before.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "What! are you back again?" he asked, in surprise.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "But I thought you had gone to visit the Wicked Witch of the West."
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "And she let you go again?" asked the man, in wonder.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "She could not help it, for she is melted," explained the Scarecrow.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "Melted! Well, that is good news, indeed," said the man. "Who melted her?"
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "Good gracious!" exclaimed the man, and he bowed very low indeed before her.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: Then he led them into his little room and locked the spectacles from the great box on all their eyes, just as he had done before. Afterward they passed on through the gate into the Emerald City. When the people heard from the Guardian of the Gates that Dorothy had melted the Wicked Witch of the West, they all gathered around the travelers and followed them in a great crowd to the Palace of Oz.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: The soldier with the green whiskers was still on guard before the door, but he let them in at once, and they were again met by the beautiful green girl, who showed each of them to their old rooms at once, so they might rest until the Great Oz was ready to receive them.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: The four travelers passed a sleepless night, each thinking of the gift Oz had promised to bestow on him. Dorothy fell asleep only once, and then she dreamed she was in Kansas, where Aunt Em was telling her how glad she was to have her little girl at home again.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: Promptly at nine o'clock the next morning the green-whiskered soldier came to them, and four minutes later they all went into the Throne Room of the Great Oz.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: Of course each one of them expected to see the Wizard in the shape he had taken before, and all were greatly surprised when they looked about and saw no one at all in the room. They kept close to the door and closer to one another, for the stillness of the empty room was more dreadful than any of the forms they had seen Oz take.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "I am Oz, the Great and Terrible. Why do you seek me?"
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: They looked again in every part of the room, and then, seeing no one, Dorothy asked, "Where are you?"
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "You promised to send me back to Kansas when the Wicked Witch was destroyed," said the girl.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "And you promised to give me brains," said the Scarecrow.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "And you promised to give me a heart," said the Tin Woodman.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "And you promised to give me courage," said the Cowardly Lion.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "Is the Wicked Witch really destroyed?" asked the Voice, and Dorothy thought it trembled a little.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "Yes," she answered, "I melted her with a bucket of water."
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "Dear me," said the Voice, "how sudden! Well, come to me tomorrow, for I must have time to think it over."
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "You've had plenty of time already," said the Tin Woodman angrily.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "We shan't wait a day longer," said the Scarecrow.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "You must keep your promises to us!" exclaimed Dorothy.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: The Lion thought it might be as well to frighten the Wizard, so he gave a large, loud roar, which was so fierce and dreadful that Toto jumped away from him in alarm and tipped over the screen that stood in a corner. As it fell with a crash they looked that way, and the next moment all of them were filled with wonder. For they saw, standing in just the spot the screen had hidden, a little old man, with a bald head and a wrinkled face, who seemed to be as much surprised as they were. The Tin Woodman, raising his axe, rushed toward the little man and cried out, "Who are you?"
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "I am Oz, the Great and Terrible," said the little man, in a trembling voice. "But don't strike me - please don't - and I'll do anything you want me to."
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: Our friends looked at him in surprise and dismay.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "I thought Oz was a great Head," said Dorothy.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "And I thought Oz was a lovely Lady," said the Scarecrow.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "And I thought Oz was a terrible Beast," said the Tin Woodman.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "And I thought Oz was a Ball of Fire," exclaimed the Lion.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "No, you are all wrong," said the little man meekly. "I have been making believe."
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "Making believe!" cried Dorothy. "Are you not a Great Wizard?"
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "Hush, my dear," he said. "Don't speak so loud, or you will be overheard - and I should be ruined. I'm supposed to be a Great Wizard."
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "Not a bit of it, my dear; I'm just a common man."
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "You're more than that," said the Scarecrow, in a grieved tone; "you're a humbug."
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "Exactly so!" declared the little man, rubbing his hands together as if it pleased him. "I am a humbug."
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "But this is terrible," said the Tin Woodman. "How shall I ever get my heart?"
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "Or I my brains?" wailed the Scarecrow, wiping the tears from his eyes with his coat sleeve.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "My dear friends," said Oz, "I pray you not to speak of these little things. Think of me, and the terrible trouble I'm in at being found out."
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "Doesn't anyone else know you're a humbug?" asked Dorothy.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "No one knows it but you four - and myself," replied Oz. "I have fooled everyone so long that I thought I should never be found out. It was a great mistake my ever letting you into the Throne Room. Usually I will not see even my subjects, and so they believe I am something terrible."
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "But, I don't understand," said Dorothy, in bewilderment. "How was it that you appeared to me as a great Head?"
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "That was one of my tricks," answered Oz. "Step this way, please, and I will tell you all about it."
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: He led the way to a small chamber in the rear of the Throne Room, and they all followed him. He pointed to one corner, in which lay the great Head, made out of many thicknesses of paper, and with a carefully painted face.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "This I hung from the ceiling by a wire," said Oz. "I stood behind the screen and pulled a thread, to make the eyes move and the mouth open."
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "Oh, I am a ventriloquist," said the little man. "I can throw the sound of my voice wherever I wish, so that you thought it was coming out of the Head. Here are the other things I used to deceive you." He showed the Scarecrow the dress and the mask he had worn when he seemed to be the lovely Lady. And the Tin Woodman saw that his terrible Beast was nothing but a lot of skins, sewn together, with slats to keep their sides out. As for the Ball of Fire, the false Wizard had hung that also from the ceiling. It was really a ball of cotton, but when oil was poured upon it the ball burned fiercely.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "Really," said the Scarecrow, "you ought to be ashamed of yourself for being such a humbug."
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "I am - I certainly am," answered the little man sorrowfully; "but it was the only thing I could do. Sit down, please, there are plenty of chairs; and I will tell you my story."
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: So they sat down and listened while he told the following tale.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "Why, that isn't very far from Kansas!" cried Dorothy.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "No, but it's farther from here," he said, shaking his head at her sadly. "When I grew up I became a ventriloquist, and at that I was very well trained by a great master. I can imitate any kind of a bird or beast." Here he mewed so like a kitten that Toto pricked up his ears and looked everywhere to see where she was. "After a time," continued Oz, "I tired of that, and became a balloonist."
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "A man who goes up in a balloon on circus day, so as to draw a crowd of people together and get them to pay to see the circus," he explained.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "Well, one day I went up in a balloon and the ropes got twisted, so that I couldn't come down again. It went way up above the clouds, so far that a current of air struck it and carried it many, many miles away. For a day and a night I traveled through the air, and on the morning of the second day I awoke and found the balloon floating over a strange and beautiful country.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "It came down gradually, and I was not hurt a bit. But I found myself in the midst of a strange people, who, seeing me come from the clouds, thought I was a great Wizard. Of course I let them think so, because they were afraid of me, and promised to do anything I wished them to.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "Just to amuse myself, and keep the good people busy, I ordered them to build this City, and my Palace; and they did it all willingly and well. Then I thought, as the country was so green and beautiful, I would call it the Emerald City; and to make the name fit better I put green spectacles on all the people, so that everything they saw was green."
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "But isn't everything here green?" asked Dorothy.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "No more than in any other city," replied Oz; "but when you wear green spectacles, why of course everything you see looks green to you. The Emerald City was built a great many years ago, for I was a young man when the balloon brought me here, and I am a very old man now. But my people have worn green glasses on their eyes so long that most of them think it really is an Emerald City, and it certainly is a beautiful place, abounding in jewels and precious metals, and every good thing that is needed to make one happy. I have been good to the people, and they like me; but ever since this Palace was built, I have shut myself up and would not see any of them.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "I think you are a very bad man," said Dorothy.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "Oh, no, my dear; I'm really a very good man, but I'm a very bad Wizard, I must admit."
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "Can't you give me brains?" asked the Scarecrow.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "You don't need them. You are learning something every day. A baby has brains, but it doesn't know much. Experience is the only thing that brings knowledge, and the longer you are on earth the more experience you are sure to get."
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "That may all be true," said the Scarecrow, "but I shall be very unhappy unless you give me brains."
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "Well," he said with a sigh, "I'm not much of a magician, as I said; but if you will come to me tomorrow morning, I will stuff your head with brains. I cannot tell you how to use them, however; you must find that out for yourself."
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "Oh, thank you - thank you!" cried the Scarecrow. "I'll find a way to use them, never fear!"
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "But how about my courage?" asked the Lion anxiously.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "You have plenty of courage, I am sure," answered Oz. "All you need is confidence in yourself. There is no living thing that is not afraid when it faces danger. The True courage is in facing danger when you are afraid, and that kind of courage you have in plenty."
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "Perhaps I have, but I'm scared just the same," said the Lion. "I shall really be very unhappy unless you give me the sort of courage that makes one forget he is afraid."
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "Very well, I will give you that sort of courage tomorrow," replied Oz.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "Why, as for that," answered Oz, "I think you are wrong to want a heart. It makes most people unhappy. If you only knew it, you are in luck not to have a heart."
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "That must be a matter of opinion," said the Tin Woodman. "For my part, I will bear all the unhappiness without a murmur, if you will give me the heart."
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "Very well," answered Oz meekly. "Come to me tomorrow and you shall have a heart. I have played Wizard for so many years that I may as well continue the part a little longer."
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "And now," said Dorothy, "how am I to get back to Kansas?"
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "We shall have to think about that," replied the little man. "Give me two or three days to consider the matter and I'll try to find a way to carry you over the desert. In the meantime you shall all be treated as my guests, and while you live in the Palace my people will wait upon you and obey your slightest wish. There is only one thing I ask in return for my help - such as it is. You must keep my secret and tell no one I am a humbug."
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: They agreed to say nothing of what they had learned, and went back to their rooms in high spirits. Even Dorothy had hope that "The Great and Terrible Humbug," as she called him, would find a way to send her back to Kansas, and if he did she was willing to forgive him everything.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "Congratulate me. I am going to Oz to get my brains at last. When I return I shall be as other men are."
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "I have always liked you as you were," said Dorothy simply.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "It is kind of you to like a Scarecrow," he replied. "But surely you will think more of me when you hear the splendid thoughts my new brain is going to turn out." Then he said good-bye to them all in a cheerful voice and went to the Throne Room, where he rapped upon the door.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: The Scarecrow went in and found the little man sitting down by the window, engaged in deep thought.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "I have come for my brains," remarked the Scarecrow, a little uneasily.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "Oh, yes; sit down in that chair, please," replied Oz. "You must excuse me for taking your head off, but I shall have to do it in order to put your brains in their proper place."
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "That's all right," said the Scarecrow. "You are quite welcome to take my head off, as long as it will be a better one when you put it on again."
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: So the Wizard unfastened his head and emptied out the straw. Then he entered the back room and took up a measure of bran, which he mixed with a great many pins and needles. Having shaken them together thoroughly, he filled the top of the Scarecrow's head with the mixture and stuffed the rest of the space with straw, to hold it in place.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: When he had fastened the Scarecrow's head on his body again he said to him, "Hereafter you will be a great man, for I have given you a lot of bran-new brains."
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: The Scarecrow was both pleased and proud at the fulfillment of his greatest wish, and having thanked Oz warmly he went back to his friends.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: Dorothy looked at him curiously. His head was quite bulged out at the top with brains.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "I feel wise indeed," he answered earnestly. "When I get used to my brains I shall know everything."
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "Why are those needles and pins sticking out of your head?" asked the Tin Woodman.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "That is proof that he is sharp," remarked the Lion.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "Well, I must go to Oz and get my heart," said the Woodman. So he walked to the Throne Room and knocked at the door.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "Come in," called Oz, and the Woodman entered and said, "I have come for my heart."
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "Very well," answered the little man. "But I shall have to cut a hole in your breast, so I can put your heart in the right place. I hope it won't hurt you."
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "Oh, no," answered the Woodman. "I shall not feel it at all."
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: So Oz brought a pair of tinsmith's shears and cut a small, square hole in the left side of the Tin Woodman's breast. Then, going to a chest of drawers, he took out a pretty heart, made entirely of silk and stuffed with sawdust.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "It is, indeed!" replied the Woodman, who was greatly pleased. "But is it a kind heart?"
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "Oh, very!" answered Oz. He put the heart in the Woodman's breast and then replaced the square of tin, soldering it neatly together where it had been cut.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "There," said he; "now you have a heart that any man might be proud of. I'm sorry I had to put a patch on your breast, but it really couldn't be helped."
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "Never mind the patch," exclaimed the happy Woodman. "I am very grateful to you, and shall never forget your kindness."
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: Then the Tin Woodman went back to his friends, who wished him every joy on account of his good fortune.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: The Lion now walked to the Throne Room and knocked at the door.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "I have come for my courage," announced the Lion, entering the room.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "Very well," answered the little man; "I will get it for you."
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "Well," answered Oz, "if it were inside of you, it would be courage. You know, of course, that courage is always inside one; so that this really cannot be called courage until you have swallowed it. Therefore I advise you to drink it as soon as possible."
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: The Lion hesitated no longer, but drank till the dish was empty.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "Full of courage," replied the Lion, who went joyfully back to his friends to tell them of his good fortune.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: Oz, left to himself, smiled to think of his success in giving the Scarecrow and the Tin Woodman and the Lion exactly what they thought they wanted. "How can I help being a humbug," he said, "when all these people make me do things that everybody knows can't be done? It was easy to make the Scarecrow and the Lion and the Woodman happy, because they imagined I could do anything. But it will take more than imagination to carry Dorothy back to Kansas, and I'm sure I don't know how it can be done."
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: For three days Dorothy heard nothing from Oz. These were sad days for the little girl, although her friends were all quite happy and contented. The Scarecrow told them there were wonderful thoughts in his head; but he would not say what they were because he knew no one could understand them but himself. When the Tin Woodman walked about he felt his heart rattling around in his breast; and he told Dorothy he had discovered it to be a kinder and more tender heart than the one he had owned when he was made of flesh. The Lion declared he was afraid of nothing on earth, and would gladly face an army or a dozen of the fierce Kalidahs.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: Thus each of the little party was satisfied except Dorothy, who longed more than ever to get back to Kansas.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "Sit down, my dear; I think I have found the way to get you out of this country."
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "Well, I'm not sure about Kansas," said Oz, "for I haven't the faintest notion which way it lies. But the first thing to do is to cross the desert, and then it should be easy to find your way home."
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "Well, I'll tell you what I think," said the little man. "You see, when I came to this country it was in a balloon. You also came through the air, being carried by a cyclone. So I believe the best way to get across the desert will be through the air. Now, it is quite beyond my powers to make a cyclone; but I've been thinking the matter over, and I believe I can make a balloon."
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "A balloon," said Oz, "is made of silk, which is coated with glue to keep the gas in it. I have plenty of silk in the Palace, so it will be no trouble to make the balloon. But in all this country there is no gas to fill the balloon with, to make it float."
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "If it won't float," remarked Dorothy, "it will be of no use to us."
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "True," answered Oz. "But there is another way to make it float, which is to fill it with hot air. Hot air isn't as good as gas, for if the air should get cold the balloon would come down in the desert, and we should be lost."
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "We!" exclaimed the girl. "Are you going with me?"
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "Yes, of course," replied Oz. "I am tired of being such a humbug. If I should go out of this Palace my people would soon discover I am not a Wizard, and then they would be vexed with me for having deceived them. So I have to stay shut up in these rooms all day, and it gets tiresome. I'd much rather go back to Kansas with you and be in a circus again."
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "I shall be glad to have your company," said Dorothy.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "Thank you," he answered. "Now, if you will help me sew the silk together, we will begin to work on our balloon."
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: So Dorothy took a needle and thread, and as fast as Oz cut the strips of silk into proper shape the girl sewed them neatly together. First there was a strip of light green silk, then a strip of dark green and then a strip of emerald green; for Oz had a fancy to make the balloon in different shades of the color about them. It took three days to sew all the strips together, but when it was finished they had a big bag of green silk more than twenty feet long.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: Then Oz painted it on the inside with a coat of thin glue, to make it airtight, after which he announced that the balloon was ready.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "But we must have a basket to ride in," he said. So he sent the soldier with the green whiskers for a big clothes basket, which he fastened with many ropes to the bottom of the balloon.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: When it was all ready, Oz sent word to his people that he was going to make a visit to a great brother Wizard who lived in the clouds. The news spread rapidly throughout the city and everyone came to see the wonderful sight.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: Oz ordered the balloon carried out in front of the Palace, and the people gazed upon it with much curiosity. The Tin Woodman had chopped a big pile of wood, and now he made a fire of it, and Oz held the bottom of the balloon over the fire so that the hot air that arose from it would be caught in the silken bag. Gradually the balloon swelled out and rose into the air, until finally the basket just touched the ground.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "I am now going away to make a visit. While I am gone the Scarecrow will rule over you. I command you to obey him as you would me."
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: The balloon was by this time tugging hard at the rope that held it to the ground, for the air within it was hot, and this made it so much lighter in weight than the air without that it pulled hard to rise into the sky.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "Come, Dorothy!" cried the Wizard. "Hurry up, or the balloon will fly away."
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "I can't find Toto anywhere," replied Dorothy, who did not wish to leave her little dog behind. Toto had run into the crowd to bark at a kitten, and Dorothy at last found him. She picked him up and ran towards the balloon.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: She was within a few steps of it, and Oz was holding out his hands to help her into the basket, when, crack! went the ropes, and the balloon rose into the air without her.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "Come back!" she screamed. "I want to go, too!"
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "I can't come back, my dear," called Oz from the basket. "Good-bye!"
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "Good-bye!" shouted everyone, and all eyes were turned upward to where the Wizard was riding in the basket, rising every moment farther and farther into the sky.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "Oz was always our friend. When he was here he built for us this beautiful Emerald City, and now he is gone he has left the Wise Scarecrow to rule over us."
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: Still, for many days they grieved over the loss of the Wonderful Wizard, and would not be comforted.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: Dorothy wept bitterly at the passing of her hope to get home to Kansas again; but when she thought it all over she was glad she had not gone up in a balloon. And she also felt sorry at losing Oz, and so did her companions.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "Truly I should be ungrateful if I failed to mourn for the man who gave me my lovely heart. I should like to cry a little because Oz is gone, if you will kindly wipe away my tears, so that I shall not rust."
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "With pleasure," she answered, and brought a towel at once. Then the Tin Woodman wept for several minutes, and she watched the tears carefully and wiped them away with the towel. When he had finished, he thanked her kindly and oiled himself thoroughly with his jeweled oil-can, to guard against mishap.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: The Scarecrow was now the ruler of the Emerald City, and although he was not a Wizard the people were proud of him. "For," they said, "there is not another city in all the world that is ruled by a stuffed man." And, so far as they knew, they were quite right.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: The morning after the balloon had gone up with Oz, the four travelers met in the Throne Room and talked matters over. The Scarecrow sat in the big throne and the others stood respectfully before him.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "We are not so unlucky," said the new ruler, "for this Palace and the Emerald City belong to us, and we can do just as we please. When I remember that a short time ago I was up on a pole in a farmer's cornfield, and that now I am the ruler of this beautiful City, I am quite satisfied with my lot."
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "I also," said the Tin Woodman, "am well-pleased with my new heart; and, really, that was the only thing I wished in all the world."
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "For my part, I am content in knowing I am as brave as any beast that ever lived, if not braver," said the Lion modestly.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "If Dorothy would only be contented to live in the Emerald City," continued the Scarecrow, "we might all be happy together."
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "But I don't want to live here," cried Dorothy. "I want to go to Kansas, and live with Aunt Em and Uncle Henry."
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "Well, then, what can be done?" inquired the Woodman.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "Why not call the Winged Monkeys, and ask them to carry you over the desert?"
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "I never thought of that!" said Dorothy joyfully. "It's just the thing. I'll go at once for the Golden Cap."
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: When she brought it into the Throne Room she spoke the magic words, and soon the band of Winged Monkeys flew in through the open window and stood beside her.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "This is the second time you have called us," said the Monkey King, bowing before the little girl. "What do you wish?"
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "I want you to fly with me to Kansas," said Dorothy.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "That cannot be done," he said. "We belong to this country alone, and cannot leave it. There has never been a Winged Monkey in Kansas yet, and I suppose there never will be, for they don't belong there. We shall be glad to serve you in any way in our power, but we cannot cross the desert. Good-bye."
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: And with another bow, the Monkey King spread his wings and flew away through the window, followed by all his band.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: Dorothy was ready to cry with disappointment. "I have wasted the charm of the Golden Cap to no purpose," she said, "for the Winged Monkeys cannot help me."
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "It is certainly too bad!" said the tender-hearted Woodman.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: The Scarecrow was thinking again, and his head bulged out so horribly that Dorothy feared it would burst.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "Let us call in the soldier with the green whiskers," he said, "and ask his advice."
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: So the soldier was summoned and entered the Throne Room timidly, for while Oz was alive he never was allowed to come farther than the door.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "This little girl," said the Scarecrow to the soldier, "wishes to cross the desert. How can she do so?"
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "I cannot tell," answered the soldier, "for nobody has ever crossed the desert, unless it is Oz himself."
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "Is there no one who can help me?" asked Dorothy earnestly.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "The Witch of the South. She is the most powerful of all the Witches, and rules over the Quadlings. Besides, her castle stands on the edge of the desert, so she may know a way to cross it."
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "Glinda is a Good Witch, isn't she?" asked the child.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "The Quadlings think she is good," said the soldier, "and she is kind to everyone. I have heard that Glinda is a beautiful woman, who knows how to keep young in spite of the many years she has lived."
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "How can I get to her castle?" asked Dorothy.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "The road is straight to the South," he answered, "but it is said to be full of dangers to travelers. There are wild beasts in the woods, and a race of queer men who do not like strangers to cross their country. For this reason none of the Quadlings ever come to the Emerald City."
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "It seems, in spite of dangers, that the best thing Dorothy can do is to travel to the Land of the South and ask Glinda to help her. For, of course, if Dorothy stays here she will never get back to Kansas."
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "You must have been thinking again," remarked the Tin Woodman.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "I shall go with Dorothy," declared the Lion, "for I am tired of your city and long for the woods and the country again. I am really a wild beast, you know. Besides, Dorothy will need someone to protect her."
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "That is true," agreed the Woodman. "My axe may be of service to her; so I also will go with her to the Land of the South."
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "Certainly. If it wasn't for Dorothy I should never have had brains. She lifted me from the pole in the cornfield and brought me to the Emerald City. So my good luck is all due to her, and I shall never leave her until she starts back to Kansas for good and all."
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "Thank you," said Dorothy gratefully. "You are all very kind to me. But I should like to start as soon as possible."
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "We shall go tomorrow morning," returned the Scarecrow. "So now let us all get ready, for it will be a long journey."
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: The next morning Dorothy kissed the pretty green girl good-bye, and they all shook hands with the soldier with the green whiskers, who had walked with them as far as the gate. When the Guardian of the Gate saw them again he wondered greatly that they could leave the beautiful City to get into new trouble. But he at once unlocked their spectacles, which he put back into the green box, and gave them many good wishes to carry with them.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "You are now our ruler," he said to the Scarecrow; "so you must come back to us as soon as possible."
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "I certainly shall if I am able," the Scarecrow replied; "but I must help Dorothy to get home, first."
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "I have been very kindly treated in your lovely City, and everyone has been good to me. I cannot tell you how grateful I am."
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "Don't try, my dear," he answered. "We should like to keep you with us, but if it is your wish to return to Kansas, I hope you will find a way." He then opened the gate of the outer wall, and they walked forth and started upon their journey.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: The sun shone brightly as our friends turned their faces toward the Land of the South. They were all in the best of spirits, and laughed and chatted together. Dorothy was once more filled with the hope of getting home, and the Scarecrow and the Tin Woodman were glad to be of use to her. As for the Lion, he sniffed the fresh air with delight and whisked his tail from side to side in pure joy at being in the country again, while Toto ran around them and chased the moths and butterflies, barking merrily all the time.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "City life does not agree with me at all," remarked the Lion, as they walked along at a brisk pace. "I have lost much flesh since I lived there, and now I am anxious for a chance to show the other beasts how courageous I have grown."
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: They now turned and took a last look at the Emerald City. All they could see was a mass of towers and steeples behind the green walls, and high up above everything the spires and dome of the Palace of Oz.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "Oz was not such a bad Wizard, after all," said the Tin Woodman, as he felt his heart rattling around in his breast.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "He knew how to give me brains, and very good brains, too," said the Scarecrow.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "If Oz had taken a dose of the same courage he gave me," added the Lion, "he would have been a brave man."
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: Dorothy said nothing. Oz had not kept the promise he made her, but he had done his best, so she forgave him. As he said, he was a good man, even if he was a bad Wizard.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: The first day's journey was through the green fields and bright flowers that stretched about the Emerald City on every side. They slept that night on the grass, with nothing but the stars over them; and they rested very well indeed.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: In the morning they traveled on until they came to a thick wood. There was no way of going around it, for it seemed to extend to the right and left as far as they could see; and, besides, they did not dare change the direction of their journey for fear of getting lost. So they looked for the place where it would be easiest to get into the forest.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: The Scarecrow, who was in the lead, finally discovered a big tree with such wide-spreading branches that there was room for the party to pass underneath. So he walked forward to the tree, but just as he came under the first branches they bent down and twined around him, and the next minute he was raised from the ground and flung headlong among his fellow travelers.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: This did not hurt the Scarecrow, but it surprised him, and he looked rather dizzy when Dorothy picked him up.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "Here is another space between the trees," called the Lion.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "Let me try it first," said the Scarecrow, "for it doesn't hurt me to get thrown about." He walked up to another tree, as he spoke, but its branches immediately seized him and tossed him back again.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "This is strange," exclaimed Dorothy. "What shall we do?"
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "The trees seem to have made up their minds to fight us, and stop our journey," remarked the Lion.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "I believe I will try it myself," said the Woodman, and shouldering his axe, he marched up to the first tree that had handled the Scarecrow so roughly. When a big branch bent down to seize him the Woodman chopped at it so fiercely that he cut it in two. At once the tree began shaking all its branches as if in pain, and the Tin Woodman passed safely under it.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "Come on!" he shouted to the others. "Be quick!" They all ran forward and passed under the tree without injury, except Toto, who was caught by a small branch and shaken until he howled. But the Woodman promptly chopped off the branch and set the little dog free.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: The other trees of the forest did nothing to keep them back, so they made up their minds that only the first row of trees could bend down their branches, and that probably these were the policemen of the forest, and given this wonderful power in order to keep strangers out of it.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: The four travelers walked with ease through the trees until they came to the farther edge of the wood. Then, to their surprise, they found before them a high wall which seemed to be made of white china. It was smooth, like the surface of a dish, and higher than their heads.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "I will make a ladder," said the Tin Woodman, "for we certainly must climb over the wall."
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: While the Woodman was making a ladder from wood which he found in the forest Dorothy lay down and slept, for she was tired by the long walk. The Lion also curled himself up to sleep and Toto lay beside him.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "I cannot think why this wall is here, nor what it is made of."
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "Rest your brains and do not worry about the wall," replied the Woodman. "When we have climbed over it, we shall know what is on the other side."
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: After a time the ladder was finished. It looked clumsy, but the Tin Woodman was sure it was strong and would answer their purpose. The Scarecrow waked Dorothy and the Lion and Toto, and told them that the ladder was ready. The Scarecrow climbed up the ladder first, but he was so awkward that Dorothy had to follow close behind and keep him from falling off. When he got his head over the top of the wall the Scarecrow said, "Oh, my!"
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: So the Scarecrow climbed farther up and sat down on the top of the wall, and Dorothy put her head over and cried, "Oh, my!" just as the Scarecrow had done.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: Then Toto came up, and immediately began to bark, but Dorothy made him be still.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: The Lion climbed the ladder next, and the Tin Woodman came last; but both of them cried, "Oh, my!" as soon as they looked over the wall. When they were all sitting in a row on the top of the wall, they looked down and saw a strange sight.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: Before them was a great stretch of country having a floor as smooth and shining and white as the bottom of a big platter. Scattered around were many houses made entirely of china and painted in the brightest colors. These houses were quite small, the biggest of them reaching only as high as Dorothy's waist. There were also pretty little barns, with china fences around them; and many cows and sheep and horses and pigs and chickens, all made of china, were standing about in groups.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: No one did so much as look at the travelers at first, except one little purple china dog with an extra-large head, which came to the wall and barked at them in a tiny voice, afterwards running away again.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: They found the ladder so heavy they could not pull it up, so the Scarecrow fell off the wall and the others jumped down upon him so that the hard floor would not hurt their feet. Of course they took pains not to light on his head and get the pins in their feet. When all were safely down they picked up the Scarecrow, whose body was quite flattened out, and patted his straw into shape again.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "We must cross this strange place in order to get to the other side," said Dorothy, "for it would be unwise for us to go any other way except due South."
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: They began walking through the country of the china people, and the first thing they came to was a china milkmaid milking a china cow. As they drew near, the cow suddenly gave a kick and kicked over the stool, the pail, and even the milkmaid herself, and all fell on the china ground with a great clatter.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: Dorothy was shocked to see that the cow had broken her leg off, and that the pail was lying in several small pieces, while the poor milkmaid had a nick in her left elbow.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "There!" cried the milkmaid angrily. "See what you have done! My cow has broken her leg, and I must take her to the mender's shop and have it glued on again. What do you mean by coming here and frightening my cow?"
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "I'm very sorry," returned Dorothy. "Please forgive us."
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: But the pretty milkmaid was much too vexed to make any answer. She picked up the leg sulkily and led her cow away, the poor animal limping on three legs. As she left them the milkmaid cast many reproachful glances over her shoulder at the clumsy strangers, holding her nicked elbow close to her side.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "We must be very careful here," said the kind-hearted Woodman, "or we may hurt these pretty little people so they will never get over it."
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: A little farther on Dorothy met a most beautifully dressed young Princess, who stopped short as she saw the strangers and started to run away.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: She had such a frightened little voice that Dorothy stopped and said, "Why not?"
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "Because," answered the Princess, also stopping, a safe distance away, "if I run I may fall down and break myself."
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "But could you not be mended?" asked the girl.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "Oh, yes; but one is never so pretty after being mended, you know," replied the Princess.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "Now there is Mr. Joker, one of our clowns," continued the china lady, "who is always trying to stand upon his head. He has broken himself so often that he is mended in a hundred places, and doesn't look at all pretty. Here he comes now, so you can see for yourself."
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: Indeed, a jolly little clown came walking toward them, and Dorothy could see that in spite of his pretty clothes of red and yellow and green he was completely covered with cracks, running every which way and showing plainly that he had been mended in many places.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "My lady fair, Why do you stare At poor old Mr. Joker? You're quite as stiff And prim as if You'd eaten up a poker!"
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "Be quiet, sir!" said the Princess. "Can't you see these are strangers, and should be treated with respect?"
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "Well, that's respect, I expect," declared the Clown, and immediately stood upon his head.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "Don't mind Mr. Joker," said the Princess to Dorothy. "He is considerably cracked in his head, and that makes him foolish."
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "Oh, I don't mind him a bit," said Dorothy. "But you are so beautiful," she continued, "that I am sure I could love you dearly. Won't you let me carry you back to Kansas, and stand you on Aunt Em's mantel? I could carry you in my basket."
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "That would make me very unhappy," answered the china Princess. "You see, here in our country we live contentedly, and can talk and move around as we please. But whenever any of us are taken away our joints at once stiffen, and we can only stand straight and look pretty. Of course that is all that is expected of us when we are on mantels and cabinets and drawing-room tables, but our lives are much pleasanter here in our own country."
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "I would not make you unhappy for all the world!" exclaimed Dorothy. "So I'll just say good-bye."
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: They walked carefully through the china country. The little animals and all the people scampered out of their way, fearing the strangers would break them, and after an hour or so the travelers reached the other side of the country and came to another china wall.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: It was not so high as the first, however, and by standing upon the Lion's back they all managed to scramble to the top. Then the Lion gathered his legs under him and jumped on the wall; but just as he jumped, he upset a china church with his tail and smashed it all to pieces.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "That was too bad," said Dorothy, "but really I think we were lucky in not doing these little people more harm than breaking a cow's leg and a church. They are all so brittle!"
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "They are, indeed," said the Scarecrow, "and I am thankful I am made of straw and cannot be easily damaged. There are worse things in the world than being a Scarecrow."
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: After climbing down from the china wall the travelers found themselves in a disagreeable country, full of bogs and marshes and covered with tall, rank grass. It was difficult to walk without falling into muddy holes, for the grass was so thick that it hid them from sight. However, by carefully picking their way, they got safely along until they reached solid ground. But here the country seemed wilder than ever, and after a long and tiresome walk through the underbrush they entered another forest, where the trees were bigger and older than any they had ever seen.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "This forest is perfectly delightful," declared the Lion, looking around him with joy. "Never have I seen a more beautiful place."
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "Not a bit of it," answered the Lion. "I should like to live here all my life. See how soft the dried leaves are under your feet and how rich and green the moss is that clings to these old trees. Surely no wild beast could wish a pleasanter home."
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "Perhaps there are wild beasts in the forest now," said Dorothy.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "I suppose there are," returned the Lion, "but I do not see any of them about."
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: They walked through the forest until it became too dark to go any farther. Dorothy and Toto and the Lion lay down to sleep, while the Woodman and the Scarecrow kept watch over them as usual.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: When morning came, they started again. Before they had gone far they heard a low rumble, as of the growling of many wild animals. Toto whimpered a little, but none of the others was frightened, and they kept along the well-trodden path until they came to an opening in the wood, in which were gathered hundreds of beasts of every variety. There were tigers and elephants and bears and wolves and foxes and all the others in the natural history, and for a moment Dorothy was afraid. But the Lion explained that the animals were holding a meeting, and he judged by their snarling and growling that they were in great trouble.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "Welcome, O King of Beasts! You have come in good time to fight our enemy and bring peace to all the animals of the forest once more."
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "What is your trouble?" asked the Lion quietly.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "We are all threatened," answered the tiger, "by a fierce enemy which has lately come into this forest. It is a most tremendous monster, like a great spider, with a body as big as an elephant and legs as long as a tree trunk. It has eight of these long legs, and as the monster crawls through the forest he seizes an animal with a leg and drags it to his mouth, where he eats it as a spider does a fly. Not one of us is safe while this fierce creature is alive, and we had called a meeting to decide how to take care of ourselves when you came among us."
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "Are there any other lions in this forest?" he asked.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "No; there were some, but the monster has eaten them all. And, besides, they were none of them nearly so large and brave as you."
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "If I put an end to your enemy, will you bow down to me and obey me as King of the Forest?" inquired the Lion.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "We will do that gladly," returned the tiger; and all the other beasts roared with a mighty roar: "We will!"
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "Where is this great spider of yours now?" asked the Lion.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "Yonder, among the oak trees," said the tiger, pointing with his forefoot.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "Take good care of these friends of mine," said the Lion, "and I will go at once to fight the monster."
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: He bade his comrades good-bye and marched proudly away to do battle with the enemy.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: Then the beasts bowed down to the Lion as their King, and he promised to come back and rule over them as soon as Dorothy was safely on her way to Kansas.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: The four travelers passed through the rest of the forest in safety, and when they came out from its gloom saw before them a steep hill, covered from top to bottom with great pieces of rock.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "That will be a hard climb," said the Scarecrow, "but we must get over the hill, nevertheless."
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: So he led the way and the others followed. They had nearly reached the first rock when they heard a rough voice cry out, "Keep back!"
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: Then a head showed itself over the rock and the same voice said, "This hill belongs to us, and we don't allow anyone to cross it."
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "But we must cross it," said the Scarecrow. "We're going to the country of the Quadlings."
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: "But you shall not!" replied the voice, and there stepped from behind the rock the strangest man the travelers had ever seen.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: He was quite short and stout and had a big head, which was flat at the top and supported by a thick neck full of wrinkles. But he had no arms at all, and, seeing this, the Scarecrow did not fear that so helpless a creature could prevent them from climbing the hill. So he said, "I'm sorry not to do as you wish, but we must pass over your hill whether you like it or not," and he walked boldly forward.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: As quick as lightning the man's head shot forward and his neck stretched out until the top of the head, where it was flat, struck the Scarecrow in the middle and sent him tumbling, over and over, down the hill. Almost as quickly as it came the head went back to the body, and the man laughed harshly as he said, "It isn't as easy as you think!"
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: A chorus of boisterous laughter came from the other rocks, and Dorothy saw hundreds of the armless Hammer-Heads upon the hillside, one behind every rock.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: The Lion became quite angry at the laughter caused by the Scarecrow's mishap, and giving a loud roar that echoed like thunder, he dashed up the hill.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: Again a head shot swiftly out, and the great Lion went rolling down the hill as if he had been struck by a cannon ball.
quotes.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz — L. Frank Baum

quotes.text: Dorothy ran down and helped the Scarecrow to his feet, and the Lion came up to her, feeling rather bruised and sore, and said, "It is useless to fight people with shooting heads; no one can withstand them."
