quotes.text: For two or three minutes he stood looking round him, while Mary watched him, and then he began to walk about softly, even more lightly than Mary had walked the first time she had found herself inside the four walls. His eyes seemed to be taking in everything - the gray trees with the gray creepers climbing over them and hanging from their branches, the tangle on the walls and among the grass, the evergreen alcoves with the stone seats and tall flower urns standing in them.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I never thought I'd see this place," he said at last, in a whisper.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: She had spoken aloud and he made a sign to her.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "We must talk low," he said, "or someone'll hear us an' wonder what's to do in here."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Oh! I forgot!" said Mary, feeling frightened and putting her hand quickly against her mouth. "Did you know about the garden?" she asked again when she had recovered herself.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Martha told me there was one as no one ever went inside," he answered. "Us used to wonder what it was like."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: He stopped and looked round at the lovely gray tangle about him, and his round eyes looked queerly happy.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Eh! the nests as'll be here come springtime," he said. "It'd be th' safest nestin' place in England. No one never comin' near an' tangles o' trees an' roses to build in. I wonder all th' birds on th' moor don't build here."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: Mistress Mary put her hand on his arm again without knowing it.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Will there be roses?" she whispered. "Can you tell? I thought perhaps they were all dead."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Eh! No! Not them - not all of 'em!" he answered. "Look here!"
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: He stepped over to the nearest tree - an old, old one with gray lichen all over its bark, but upholding a curtain of tangled sprays and branches. He took a thick knife out of his pocket and opened one of its blades.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "There's lots o' dead wood as ought to be cut out," he said. "An' there's a lot o' old wood, but it made some new last year. This here's a new bit," and he touched a shoot which looked brownish green instead of hard, dry gray.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: Mary touched it herself in an eager, reverent way.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "That one?" she said. "Is that one quite alive quite?"
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "It's as wick as you or me," he said; and Mary remembered that Martha had told her that "wick" meant "alive" or "lively."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I'm glad it's wick!" she cried out in her whisper. "I want them all to be wick. Let us go round the garden and count how many wick ones there are."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: She quite panted with eagerness, and Dickon was as eager as she was. They went from tree to tree and from bush to bush. Dickon carried his knife in his hand and showed her things which she thought wonderful.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "They've run wild," he said, "but th' strongest ones has fair thrived on it. The delicatest ones has died out, but th' others has growed an' growed, an' spread an' spread, till they's a wonder. See here!" and he pulled down a thick gray, dry-looking branch. "A body might think this was dead wood, but I don't believe it is - down to th' root. I'll cut it low down an' see."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: He knelt and with his knife cut the lifeless-looking branch through, not far above the earth.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "There!" he said exultantly. "I told thee so. There's green in that wood yet. Look at it."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: Mary was down on her knees before he spoke, gazing with all her might.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "When it looks a bit greenish an' juicy like that, it's wick," he explained. "When th' inside is dry an' breaks easy, like this here piece I've cut off, it's done for. There's a big root here as all this live wood sprung out of, an' if th' old wood's cut off an' it's dug round, and took care of there'll be - " he stopped and lifted his face to look up at the climbing and hanging sprays above him - "there'll be a fountain o' roses here this summer."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: They went from bush to bush and from tree to tree. He was very strong and clever with his knife and knew how to cut the dry and dead wood away, and could tell when an unpromising bough or twig had still green life in it. In the course of half an hour Mary thought she could tell too, and when he cut through a lifeless-looking branch she would cry out joyfully under her breath when she caught sight of the least shade of moist green. The spade, and hoe, and fork were very useful. He showed her how to use the fork while he dug about roots with the spade and stirred the earth and let the air in.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: They were working industriously round one of the biggest standard roses when he caught sight of something which made him utter an exclamation of surprise.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Why!" he cried, pointing to the grass a few feet away. "Who did that there?"
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: It was one of Mary's own little clearings round the pale green points.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Why, I thought tha' didn't know nothin' about gardenin'," he exclaimed.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I don't," she answered, "but they were so little, and the grass was so thick and strong, and they looked as if they had no room to breathe. So I made a place for them. I don't even know what they are."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: Dickon went and knelt down by them, smiling his wide smile.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Tha' was right," he said. "A gardener couldn't have told thee better. They'll grow now like Jack's bean-stalk. They're crocuses an' snowdrops, an' these here is narcissuses," turning to another patch, "an here's daffydowndillys. Eh! they will be a sight."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Tha' has done a lot o' work for such a little wench," he said, looking her over.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I'm growing fatter," said Mary, "and I'm growing stronger. I used always to be tired. When I dig I'm not tired at all. I like to smell the earth when it's turned up."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "It's rare good for thee," he said, nodding his head wisely. "There's naught as nice as th' smell o' good clean earth, except th' smell o' fresh growin' things when th' rain falls on 'em. I get out on th' moor many a day when it's rainin' an' I lie under a bush an' listen to th' soft swish o' drops on th' heather an' I just sniff an' sniff. My nose end fair quivers like a rabbit's, mother says."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Do you never catch cold?" inquired Mary, gazing at him wonderingly. She had never seen such a funny boy, or such a nice one.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Not me," he said, grinning. "I never ketched cold since I was born. I wasn't brought up nesh enough. I've chased about th' moor in all weathers same as th' rabbits does. Mother says I've sniffed up too much fresh air for twelve year' to ever get to sniffin' with cold. I'm as tough as a white-thorn knobstick."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: He was working all the time he was talking and Mary was following him and helping him with her fork or the trowel.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "There's a lot of work to do here!" he said once, looking about quite exultantly.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Will you come again and help me to do it?" Mary begged. "I'm sure I can help, too. I can dig and pull up weeds, and do whatever you tell me. Oh! do come, Dickon!"
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I'll come every day if tha' wants me, rain or shine," he answered stoutly. "It's the best fun I ever had in my life - shut in here an' wakenin' up a garden."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "If you will come," said Mary, "if you will help me to make it alive I'll - I don't know what I'll do," she ended helplessly. What could you do for a boy like that?
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I'll tell thee what tha'll do," said Dickon, with his happy grin. "Tha'll get fat an' tha'll get as hungry as a young fox an' tha'll learn how to talk to th' robin same as I do. Eh! we'll have a lot o' fun."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: He began to walk about, looking up in the trees and at the walls and bushes with a thoughtful expression.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I wouldn't want to make it look like a gardener's garden, all clipped an' spick an' span, would you?" he said. "It's nicer like this with things runnin' wild, an' swingin' an' catchin' hold of each other."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Don't let us make it tidy," said Mary anxiously. "It wouldn't seem like a secret garden if it was tidy."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: Dickon stood rubbing his rusty-red head with a rather puzzled look.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "It's a secret garden sure enough," he said, "but seems like someone besides th' robin must have been in it since it was shut up ten year' ago."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "But the door was locked and the key was buried," said Mary. "No one could get in."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "That's true," he answered. "It's a queer place. Seems to me as if there'd been a bit o' prunin' done here an' there, later than ten year' ago."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "But how could it have been done?" said Mary.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: He was examining a branch of a standard rose and he shook his head.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Aye! how could it!" he murmured. "With th' door locked an' th' key buried."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: Mistress Mary always felt that however many years she lived she should never forget that first morning when her garden began to grow. Of course, it did seem to begin to grow for her that morning. When Dickon began to clear places to plant seeds, she remembered what Basil had sung at her when he wanted to tease her.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Are there any flowers that look like bells?" she inquired.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Lilies o' th' valley does," he answered, digging away with the trowel, "an' there's Canterbury bells, an' campanulas."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "There's lilies o' th, valley here already; I saw 'em. They'll have growed too close an' we'll have to separate 'em, but there's plenty. Th' other ones takes two years to bloom from seed, but I can bring you some bits o' plants from our cottage garden. Why does tha' want 'em?"
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: Then Mary told him about Basil and his brothers and sisters in India and of how she had hated them and of their calling her "Mistress Mary Quite Contrary."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: 'Mistress Mary, quite contrary, How does your garden grow? With silver bells, and cockle shells, And marigolds all in a row.'
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: I just remembered it and it made me wonder if there were really flowers like silver bells."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: She frowned a little and gave her trowel a rather spiteful dig into the earth.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Eh!" he said, and as he crumbled the rich black soil she saw he was sniffing up the scent of it. "There doesn't seem to be no need for no one to be contrary when there's flowers an' such like, an' such lots o' friendly wild things runnin' about makin' homes for themselves, or buildin' nests an' singin' an' whistlin', does there?"
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: Mary, kneeling by him holding the seeds, looked at him and stopped frowning.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Dickon," she said, "you are as nice as Martha said you were. I like you, and you make the fifth person. I never thought I should like five people."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: Dickon sat up on his heels as Martha did when she was polishing the grate. He did look funny and delightful, Mary thought, with his round blue eyes and red cheeks and happy looking turned-up nose.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Only five folk as tha' likes?" he said. "Who is th' other four?"
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Your mother and Martha," Mary checked them off on her fingers, "and the robin and Ben Weatherstaff."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: Dickon laughed so that he was obliged to stifle the sound by putting his arm over his mouth.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I know tha' thinks I'm a queer lad," he said, "but I think tha' art th' queerest little lass I ever saw."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: Then Mary did a strange thing. She leaned forward and asked him a question she had never dreamed of asking anyone before. And she tried to ask it in Yorkshire because that was his language, and in India a native was always pleased if you knew his speech.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Eh!" he answered heartily, "that I does. I likes thee wonderful, an' so does th' robin, I do believe!"
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "That's two, then," said Mary. "That's two for me."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: And then they began to work harder than ever and more joyfully. Mary was startled and sorry when she heard the big clock in the courtyard strike the hour of her midday dinner.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I shall have to go," she said mournfully. "And you will have to go too, won't you?"
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "My dinner's easy to carry about with me," he said. "Mother always lets me put a bit o' somethin' in my pocket."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: He picked up his coat from the grass and brought out of a pocket a lumpy little bundle tied up in a quite clean, coarse, blue and white handkerchief. It held two thick pieces of bread with a slice of something laid between them.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "It's oftenest naught but bread," he said, "but I've got a fine slice o' fat bacon with it today."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: Mary thought it looked a queer dinner, but he seemed ready to enjoy it.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Run on an' get thy victuals," he said. "I'll be done with mine first. I'll get some more work done before I start back home."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I'll call th' robin up," he said, "and give him th' rind o' th' bacon to peck at. They likes a bit o' fat wonderful."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: Mary could scarcely bear to leave him. Suddenly it seemed as if he might be a sort of wood fairy who might be gone when she came into the garden again. He seemed too good to be true. She went slowly half-way to the door in the wall and then she stopped and went back.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Whatever happens, you - you never would tell?" she said.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: His poppy-colored cheeks were distended with his first big bite of bread and bacon, but he managed to smile encouragingly.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "If tha' was a missel thrush an' showed me where thy nest was, does tha' think I'd tell anyone? Not me," he said. "Tha' art as safe as a missel thrush."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: Mary ran so fast that she was rather out of breath when she reached her room. Her hair was ruffled on her forehead and her cheeks were bright pink. Her dinner was waiting on the table, and Martha was waiting near it.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Tha's a bit late," she said. "Where has tha' been?"
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I've seen Dickon!" said Mary. "I've seen Dickon!"
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I knew he'd come," said Martha exultantly. "How does tha' like him?"
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I think - I think he's beautiful!" said Mary in a determined voice.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: Martha looked rather taken aback but she looked pleased, too.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Well," she said, "he's th' best lad as ever was born, but us never thought he was handsome. His nose turns up too much."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "An' his eyes is so round," said Martha, a trifle doubtful. "Though they're a nice color."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I like them round," said Mary. "And they are exactly the color of the sky over the moor."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Mother says he made 'em that color with always lookin' up at th' birds an' th' clouds. But he has got a big mouth, hasn't he, now?"
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I love his big mouth," said Mary obstinately. "I wish mine were just like it."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "It'd look rare an' funny in thy bit of a face," she said. "But I knowed it would be that way when tha' saw him. How did tha' like th' seeds an' th' garden tools?"
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "How did you know he brought them?" asked Mary.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Eh! I never thought of him not bringin' 'em. He'd be sure to bring 'em if they was in Yorkshire. He's such a trusty lad."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: Mary was afraid that she might begin to ask difficult questions, but she did not. She was very much interested in the seeds and gardening tools, and there was only one moment when Mary was frightened. This was when she began to ask where the flowers were to be planted.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I haven't asked anybody yet," said Mary, hesitating.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Well, I wouldn't ask th' head gardener. He's too grand, Mr. Roach is."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I've never seen him," said Mary. "I've only seen undergardeners and Ben Weatherstaff."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "If I was you, I'd ask Ben Weatherstaff," advised Martha. "He's not half as bad as he looks, for all he's so crabbed. Mr. Craven lets him do what he likes because he was here when Mrs. Craven was alive, an' he used to make her laugh. She liked him. Perhaps he'd find you a corner somewhere out o' the way."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "If it was out of the way and no one wanted it, no one could mind my having it, could they?" Mary said anxiously.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "There wouldn't be no reason," answered Martha. "You wouldn't do no harm."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: Mary ate her dinner as quickly as she could and when she rose from the table she was going to run to her room to put on her hat again, but Martha stopped her.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I've got somethin' to tell you," she said. "I thought I'd let you eat your dinner first. Mr. Craven came back this mornin' and I think he wants to see you."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Oh!" she said. "Why! Why! He didn't want to see me when I came. I heard Pitcher say he didn't."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Well," explained Martha, "Mrs. Medlock says it's because o' mother. She was walkin' to Thwaite village an' she met him. She'd never spoke to him before, but Mrs. Craven had been to our cottage two or three times. He'd forgot, but mother hadn't an' she made bold to stop him. I don't know what she said to him about you but she said somethin' as put him in th' mind to see you before he goes away again, tomorrow."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Oh!" cried Mary, "is he going away tomorrow? I am so glad!"
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "He's goin' for a long time. He mayn't come back till autumn or winter. He's goin' to travel in foreign places. He's always doin' it."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Oh! I'm so glad - so glad!" said Mary thankfully.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: If he did not come back until winter, or even autumn, there would be time to watch the secret garden come alive. Even if he found out then and took it away from her she would have had that much at least.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: She did not finish the sentence, because the door opened, and Mrs. Medlock walked in. She had on her best black dress and cap, and her collar was fastened with a large brooch with a picture of a man's face on it. It was a colored photograph of Mr. Medlock who had died years ago, and she always wore it when she was dressed up. She looked nervous and excited.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Your hair's rough," she said quickly. "Go and brush it. Martha, help her to slip on her best dress. Mr. Craven sent me to bring her to him in his study."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: All the pink left Mary's cheeks. Her heart began to thump and she felt herself changing into a stiff, plain, silent child again. She did not even answer Mrs. Medlock, but turned and walked into her bedroom, followed by Martha. She said nothing while her dress was changed, and her hair brushed, and after she was quite tidy she followed Mrs. Medlock down the corridors, in silence. What was there for her to say? She was obliged to go and see Mr. Craven and he would not like her, and she would not like him. She knew what he would think of her.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: She was taken to a part of the house she had not been into before. At last Mrs. Medlock knocked at a door, and when someone said, "Come in," they entered the room together. A man was sitting in an armchair before the fire, and Mrs. Medlock spoke to him.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "You can go and leave her here. I will ring for you when I want you to take her away," said Mr. Craven.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: When she went out and closed the door, Mary could only stand waiting, a plain little thing, twisting her thin hands together. She could see that the man in the chair was not so much a hunchback as a man with high, rather crooked shoulders, and he had black hair streaked with white. He turned his head over his high shoulders and spoke to her.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: He was not ugly. His face would have been handsome if it had not been so miserable. He looked as if the sight of her worried and fretted him and as if he did not know what in the world to do with her.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: He rubbed his forehead fretfully as he looked her over.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I am getting fatter," Mary answered in what she knew was her stiffest way.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: What an unhappy face he had! His black eyes seemed as if they scarcely saw her, as if they were seeing something else, and he could hardly keep his thoughts upon her.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I forgot you," he said. "How could I remember you? I intended to send you a governess or a nurse, or someone of that sort, but I forgot."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Please," began Mary. "Please - " and then the lump in her throat choked her.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I am - I am too big for a nurse," said Mary. "And please - please don't make me have a governess yet."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: He rubbed his forehead again and stared at her.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "That was what the Sowerby woman said," he muttered absent-mindedly.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Is she - is she Martha's mother?" she stammered.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "She knows about children," said Mary. "She has twelve. She knows."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I want to play out of doors," Mary answered, hoping that her voice did not tremble. "I never liked it in India. It makes me hungry here, and I am getting fatter."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Mrs. Sowerby said it would do you good. Perhaps it will," he said. "She thought you had better get stronger before you had a governess."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "It makes me feel strong when I play and the wind comes over the moor," argued Mary.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Everywhere," gasped Mary. "Martha's mother sent me a skipping-rope. I skip and run - and I look about to see if things are beginning to stick up out of the earth. I don't do any harm."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Don't look so frightened," he said in a worried voice. "You could not do any harm, a child like you! You may do what you like."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: Mary put her hand up to her throat because she was afraid he might see the excited lump which she felt jump into it. She came a step nearer to him.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: Her anxious little face seemed to worry him more than ever.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Don't look so frightened," he exclaimed. "Of course you may. I am your guardian, though I am a poor one for any child. I cannot give you time or attention. I am too ill, and wretched and distracted; but I wish you to be happy and comfortable. I don't know anything about children, but Mrs. Medlock is to see that you have all you need. I sent for you today because Mrs. Sowerby said I ought to see you. Her daughter had talked about you. She thought you needed fresh air and freedom and running about."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "She knows all about children," Mary said again in spite of herself.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "She ought to," said Mr. Craven. "I thought her rather bold to stop me on the moor, but she said - Mrs. Craven had been kind to her." It seemed hard for him to speak his dead wife's name. "She is a respectable woman. Now I have seen you I think she said sensible things. Play out of doors as much as you like. It's a big place and you may go where you like and amuse yourself as you like. Is there anything you want?" as if a sudden thought had struck him. "Do you want toys, books, dolls?"
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Might I," quavered Mary, "might I have a bit of earth?"
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: In her eagerness she did not realize how queer the words would sound and that they were not the ones she had meant to say. Mr. Craven looked quite startled.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "To plant seeds in - to make things grow - to see them come alive," Mary faltered.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: He gazed at her a moment and then passed his hand quickly over his eyes.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Do you - care about gardens so much," he said slowly.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I didn't know about them in India," said Mary. "I was always ill and tired and it was too hot. I sometimes made little beds in the sand and stuck flowers in them. But here it is different."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: Mr. Craven got up and began to walk slowly across the room.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "A bit of earth," he said to himself, and Mary thought that somehow she must have reminded him of something. When he stopped and spoke to her his dark eyes looked almost soft and kind.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "You can have as much earth as you want," he said. "You remind me of someone else who loved the earth and things that grow. When you see a bit of earth you want," with something like a smile, "take it, child, and make it come alive."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "May I take it from anywhere - if it's not wanted?"
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Anywhere," he answered. "There! You must go now, I am tired." He touched the bell to call Mrs. Medlock. "Good-by. I shall be away all summer."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: Mrs. Medlock came so quickly that Mary thought she must have been waiting in the corridor.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Mrs. Medlock," Mr. Craven said to her, "now I have seen the child I understand what Mrs. Sowerby meant. She must be less delicate before she begins lessons. Give her simple, healthy food. Let her run wild in the garden. Don't look after her too much. She needs liberty and fresh air and romping about. Mrs. Sowerby is to come and see her now and then and she may sometimes go to the cottage."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: Mrs. Medlock looked pleased. She was relieved to hear that she need not "look after" Mary too much. She had felt her a tiresome charge and had indeed seen as little of her as she dared. In addition to this she was fond of Martha's mother.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Thank you, sir," she said. "Susan Sowerby and me went to school together and she's as sensible and good-hearted a woman as you'd find in a day's walk. I never had any children myself and she's had twelve, and there never was healthier or better ones. Miss Mary can get no harm from them. I'd always take Susan Sowerby's advice about children myself. She's what you might call healthy-minded - if you understand me."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I understand," Mr. Craven answered. "Take Miss Mary away now and send Pitcher to me."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: When Mrs. Medlock left her at the end of her own corridor Mary flew back to her room. She found Martha waiting there. Martha had, in fact, hurried back after she had removed the dinner service.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I can have my garden!" cried Mary. "I may have it where I like! I am not going to have a governess for a long time! Your mother is coming to see me and I may go to your cottage! He says a little girl like me could not do any harm and I may do what I like - anywhere!"
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Eh!" said Martha delightedly, "that was nice of him wasn't it?"
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Martha," said Mary solemnly, "he is really a nice man, only his face is so miserable and his forehead is all drawn together."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: She ran as quickly as she could to the garden. She had been away so much longer than she had thought she should and she knew Dickon would have to set out early on his five-mile walk. When she slipped through the door under the ivy, she saw he was not working where she had left him. The gardening tools were laid together under a tree. She ran to them, looking all round the place, but there was no Dickon to be seen. He had gone away and the secret garden was empty - except for the robin who had just flown across the wall and sat on a standard rose-bush watching her.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "He's gone," she said woefully. "Oh! was he - was he - was he only a wood fairy?"
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: Mary took the picture back to the house when she went to her supper and she showed it to Martha.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Eh!" said Martha with great pride. "I never knew our Dickon was as clever as that. That there's a picture of a missel thrush on her nest, as large as life an' twice as natural."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: Then Mary knew Dickon had meant the picture to be a message. He had meant that she might be sure he would keep her secret. Her garden was her nest and she was like a missel thrush. Oh, how she did like that queer, common boy!
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: She hoped he would come back the very next day and she fell asleep looking forward to the morning.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: But you never know what the weather will do in Yorkshire, particularly in the springtime. She was awakened in the night by the sound of rain beating with heavy drops against her window. It was pouring down in torrents and the wind was "wuthering" round the corners and in the chimneys of the huge old house. Mary sat up in bed and felt miserable and angry.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "The rain is as contrary as I ever was," she said. "It came because it knew I did not want it."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: She threw herself back on her pillow and buried her face. She did not cry, but she lay and hated the sound of the heavily beating rain, she hated the wind and its "wuthering." She could not go to sleep again. The mournful sound kept her awake because she felt mournful herself. If she had felt happy it would probably have lulled her to sleep. How it "wuthered" and how the big raindrops poured down and beat against the pane!
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "It sounds just like a person lost on the moor and wandering on and on crying," she said.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: She had been lying awake turning from side to side for about an hour, when suddenly something made her sit up in bed and turn her head toward the door listening. She listened and she listened.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "It isn't the wind now," she said in a loud whisper. "That isn't the wind. It is different. It is that crying I heard before."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: The door of her room was ajar and the sound came down the corridor, a far-off faint sound of fretful crying. She listened for a few minutes and each minute she became more and more sure. She felt as if she must find out what it was. It seemed even stranger than the secret garden and the buried key. Perhaps the fact that she was in a rebellious mood made her bold. She put her foot out of bed and stood on the floor.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I am going to find out what it is," she said. "Everybody is in bed and I don't care about Mrs. Medlock - I don't care!"
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: She pushed it open very gently and closed it behind her, and she stood in the corridor and could hear the crying quite plainly, though it was not loud. It was on the other side of the wall at her left and a few yards farther on there was a door. She could see a glimmer of light coming from beneath it. The Someone was crying in that room, and it was quite a young Someone.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: So she walked to the door and pushed it open, and there she was standing in the room!
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: It was a big room with ancient, handsome furniture in it. There was a low fire glowing faintly on the hearth and a night light burning by the side of a carved four-posted bed hung with brocade, and on the bed was lying a boy, crying fretfully.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: Mary wondered if she was in a real place or if she had fallen asleep again and was dreaming without knowing it.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: The boy had a sharp, delicate face the color of ivory and he seemed to have eyes too big for it. He had also a lot of hair which tumbled over his forehead in heavy locks and made his thin face seem smaller. He looked like a boy who had been ill, but he was crying more as if he were tired and cross than as if he were in pain.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: Mary stood near the door with her candle in her hand, holding her breath. Then she crept across the room, and, as she drew nearer, the light attracted the boy's attention and he turned his head on his pillow and stared at her, his gray eyes opening so wide that they seemed immense.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Who are you?" he said at last in a half-frightened whisper. "Are you a ghost?"
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "No, I am not," Mary answered, her own whisper sounding half frightened. "Are you one?"
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: He stared and stared and stared. Mary could not help noticing what strange eyes he had. They were agate gray and they looked too big for his face because they had black lashes all round them.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "No," he replied after waiting a moment or so. "I am Colin."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Your father!" gasped Mary. "No one ever told me he had a boy! Why didn't they?"
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Come here," he said, still keeping his strange eyes fixed on her with an anxious expression.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: She came close to the bed and he put out his hand and touched her.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "You are real, aren't you?" he said. "I have such real dreams very often. You might be one of them."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: Mary had slipped on a woolen wrapper before she left her room and she put a piece of it between his fingers.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Rub that and see how thick and warm it is," she said. "I will pinch you a little if you like, to show you how real I am. For a minute I thought you might be a dream too."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "From my own room. The wind wuthered so I couldn't go to sleep and I heard someone crying and wanted to find out who it was. What were you crying for?"
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Because I couldn't go to sleep either and my head ached. Tell me your name again."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Mary Lennox. Did no one ever tell you I had come to live here?"
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: He was still fingering the fold of her wrapper, but he began to look a little more as if he believed in her reality.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Because I should have been afraid you would see me. I won't let people see me and talk me over."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Why?" Mary asked again, feeling more mystified every moment.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Because I am like this always, ill and having to lie down. My father won't let people talk me over either. The servants are not allowed to speak about me. If I live I may be a hunchback, but I shan't live. My father hates to think I may be like him."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Oh, what a queer house this is!" Mary said. "What a queer house! Everything is a kind of secret. Rooms are locked up and gardens are locked up - and you! Have you been locked up?"
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "No. I stay in this room because I don't want to be moved out of it. It tires me too much."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Does your father come and see you?" Mary ventured.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Sometimes. Generally when I am asleep. He doesn't want to see me."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: A sort of angry shadow passed over the boy's face.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "My mother died when I was born and it makes him wretched to look at me. He thinks I don't know, but I've heard people talking. He almost hates me."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "He hates the garden, because she died," said Mary half speaking to herself.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Oh! just - just a garden she used to like," Mary stammered. "Have you been here always?"
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Nearly always. Sometimes I have been taken to places at the seaside, but I won't stay because people stare at me. I used to wear an iron thing to keep my back straight, but a grand doctor came from London to see me and said it was stupid. He told them to take it off and keep me out in the fresh air. I hate fresh air and I don't want to go out."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I didn't when first I came here," said Mary. "Why do you keep looking at me like that?"
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Because of the dreams that are so real," he answered rather fretfully. "Sometimes when I open my eyes I don't believe I'm awake."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "We're both awake," said Mary. She glanced round the room with its high ceiling and shadowy corners and dim fire-light. "It looks quite like a dream, and it's the middle of the night, and everybody in the house is asleep - everybody but us. We are wide awake."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I don't want it to be a dream," the boy said restlessly.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "If you don't like people to see you," she began, "do you want me to go away?"
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: He still held the fold of her wrapper and he gave it a little pull.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "No," he said. "I should be sure you were a dream if you went. If you are real, sit down on that big footstool and talk. I want to hear about you."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: Mary put down her candle on the table near the bed and sat down on the cushioned stool. She did not want to go away at all. She wanted to stay in the mysterious hidden-away room and talk to the mysterious boy.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: He wanted to know how long she had been at Misselthwaite; he wanted to know which corridor her room was on; he wanted to know what she had been doing; if she disliked the moor as he disliked it; where she had lived before she came to Yorkshire. She answered all these questions and many more and he lay back on his pillow and listened. He made her tell him a great deal about India and about her voyage across the ocean. She found out that because he had been an invalid he had not learned things as other children had. One of his nurses had taught him to read when he was quite little and he was always reading and looking at pictures in splendid books.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: Though his father rarely saw him when he was awake, he was given all sorts of wonderful things to amuse himself with. He never seemed to have been amused, however. He could have anything he asked for and was never made to do anything he did not like to do.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Everyone is obliged to do what pleases me," he said indifferently. "It makes me ill to be angry. No one believes I shall live to grow up."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: He said it as if he was so accustomed to the idea that it had ceased to matter to him at all. He seemed to like the sound of Mary's voice. As she went on talking he listened in a drowsy, interested way. Once or twice she wondered if he were not gradually falling into a doze. But at last he asked a question which opened up a new subject.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I am ten," answered Mary, forgetting herself for the moment, "and so are you."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "How do you know that?" he demanded in a surprised voice.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Because when you were born the garden door was locked and the key was buried. And it has been locked for ten years."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: Colin half sat up, turning toward her, leaning on his elbows.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "What garden door was locked? Who did it? Where was the key buried?" he exclaimed as if he were suddenly very much interested.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "It - it was the garden Mr. Craven hates," said Mary nervously. "He locked the door. No one - no one knew where he buried the key."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "What sort of a garden is it?" Colin persisted eagerly.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "No one has been allowed to go into it for ten years," was Mary's careful answer.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: But it was too late to be careful. He was too much like herself. He too had had nothing to think about and the idea of a hidden garden attracted him as it had attracted her. He asked question after question. Where was it? Had she never looked for the door? Had she never asked the gardeners?
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "They won't talk about it," said Mary. "I think they have been told not to answer questions."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Could you?" Mary faltered, beginning to feel frightened. If he could make people answer questions, who knew what might happen!
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Everyone is obliged to please me. I told you that," he said. "If I were to live, this place would sometime belong to me. They all know that. I would make them tell me."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: Mary had not known that she herself had been spoiled, but she could see quite plainly that this mysterious boy had been. He thought that the whole world belonged to him. How peculiar he was and how coolly he spoke of not living.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Do you think you won't live?" she asked, partly because she was curious and partly in hope of making him forget the garden.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I don't suppose I shall," he answered as indifferently as he had spoken before. "Ever since I remember anything I have heard people say I shan't. At first they thought I was too little to understand and now they think I don't hear. But I do. My doctor is my father's cousin. He is quite poor and if I die he will have all Misselthwaite when my father is dead. I should think he wouldn't want me to live."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "No," he answered, in a cross, tired fashion. "But I don't want to die. When I feel ill I lie here and think about it until I cry and cry."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I have heard you crying three times," Mary said, "but I did not know who it was. Were you crying about that?" She did so want him to forget the garden.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I dare say," he answered. "Let us talk about something else. Talk about that garden. Don't you want to see it?"
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I do," he went on persistently. "I don't think I ever really wanted to see anything before, but I want to see that garden. I want the key dug up. I want the door unlocked. I would let them take me there in my chair. That would be getting fresh air. I am going to make them open the door."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: He had become quite excited and his strange eyes began to shine like stars and looked more immense than ever.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "They have to please me," he said. "I will make them take me there and I will let you go, too."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: Mary's hands clutched each other. Everything would be spoiled - everything! Dickon would never come back. She would never again feel like a missel thrush with a safe-hidden nest.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Oh, don't - don't - don't - don't do that!" she cried out.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: He stared as if he thought she had gone crazy!
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Why?" he exclaimed. "You said you wanted to see it."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I do," she answered almost with a sob in her throat, "but if you make them open the door and take you in like that it will never be a secret again."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "A secret," he said. "What do you mean? Tell me."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: Mary's words almost tumbled over one another.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: He stopped her again as excited as she was herself.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "They are daffodils and lilies and snowdrops. They are working in the earth now - pushing up pale green points because the spring is coming."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Is the spring coming?" he said. "What is it like? You don't see it in rooms if you are ill."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "It is the sun shining on the rain and the rain falling on the sunshine, and things pushing up and working under the earth," said Mary. "If the garden was a secret and we could get into it we could watch the things grow bigger every day, and see how many roses are alive. Don't you see? Oh, don't you see how much nicer it would be if it was a secret?"
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: He dropped back on his pillow and lay there with an odd expression on his face.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I never had a secret," he said, "except that one about not living to grow up. They don't know I know that, so it is a sort of secret. But I like this kind better."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "If you won't make them take you to the garden," pleaded Mary, "perhaps - I feel almost sure I can find out how to get in sometime. And then - if the doctor wants you to go out in your chair, and if you can always do what you want to do, perhaps - perhaps we might find some boy who would push you, and we could go alone and it would always be a secret garden."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I should - like - that," he said very slowly, his eyes looking dreamy. "I should like that. I should not mind fresh air in a secret garden."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: Mary began to recover her breath and feel safer because the idea of keeping the secret seemed to please him. She felt almost sure that if she kept on talking and could make him see the garden in his mind as she had seen it he would like it so much that he could not bear to think that everybody might tramp in to it when they chose.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I'll tell you what I think it would be like, if we could go into it," she said. "It has been shut up so long things have grown into a tangle perhaps."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: He lay quite still and listened while she went on talking about the roses which might have clambered from tree to tree and hung down - about the many birds which might have built their nests there because it was so safe. And then she told him about the robin and Ben Weatherstaff, and there was so much to tell about the robin and it was so easy and safe to talk about it that she ceased to be afraid. The robin pleased him so much that he smiled until he looked almost beautiful, and at first Mary had thought that he was even plainer than herself, with his big eyes and heavy locks of hair.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I did not know birds could be like that," he said. "But if you stay in a room you never see things. What a lot of things you know. I feel as if you had been inside that garden."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: She did not know what to say, so she did not say anything. He evidently did not expect an answer and the next moment he gave her a surprise.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I am going to let you look at something," he said. "Do you see that rose-colored silk curtain hanging on the wall over the mantel-piece?"
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: Mary had not noticed it before, but she looked up and saw it. It was a curtain of soft silk hanging over what seemed to be some picture.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "There is a cord hanging from it," said Colin. "Go and pull it."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: Mary got up, much mystified, and found the cord. When she pulled it the silk curtain ran back on rings and when it ran back it uncovered a picture. It was the picture of a girl with a laughing face. She had bright hair tied up with a blue ribbon and her gay, lovely eyes were exactly like Colin's unhappy ones, agate gray and looking twice as big as they really were because of the black lashes all round them.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "She is my mother," said Colin complainingly. "I don't see why she died. Sometimes I hate her for doing it."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "If she had lived I believe I should not have been ill always," he grumbled. "I dare say I should have lived, too. And my father would not have hated to look at me. I dare say I should have had a strong back. Draw the curtain again."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: Mary did as she was told and returned to her footstool.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "She is much prettier than you," she said, "but her eyes are just like yours - at least they are the same shape and color. Why is the curtain drawn over her?"
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I made them do it," he said. "Sometimes I don't like to see her looking at me. She smiles too much when I am ill and miserable. Besides, she is mine and I don't want everyone to see her."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: There were a few moments of silence and then Mary spoke.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "What would Mrs. Medlock do if she found out that I had been here?" she inquired.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "She would do as I told her to do," he answered. "And I should tell her that I wanted you to come here and talk to me every day. I am glad you came."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "So am I," said Mary. "I will come as often as I can, but" - she hesitated - "I shall have to look every day for the garden door."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Yes, you must," said Colin, "and you can tell me about it afterward."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: He lay thinking a few minutes, as he had done before, and then he spoke again.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I think you shall be a secret, too," he said. "I will not tell them until they find out. I can always send the nurse out of the room and say that I want to be by myself. Do you know Martha?"
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Yes, I know her very well," said Mary. "She waits on me."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: He nodded his head toward the outer corridor.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "She is the one who is asleep in the other room. The nurse went away yesterday to stay all night with her sister and she always makes Martha attend to me when she wants to go out. Martha shall tell you when to come here."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: Then Mary understood Martha's troubled look when she had asked questions about the crying.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Martha knew about you all the time?" she said.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Yes; she often attends to me. The nurse likes to get away from me and then Martha comes."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I have been here a long time," said Mary. "Shall I go away now? Your eyes look sleepy."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I wish I could go to sleep before you leave me," he said rather shyly.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Shut your eyes," said Mary, drawing her footstool closer, "and I will do what my Ayah used to do in India. I will pat your hand and stroke it and sing something quite low."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I should like that perhaps," he said drowsily.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: Somehow she was sorry for him and did not want him to lie awake, so she leaned against the bed and began to stroke and pat his hand and sing a very low little chanting song in Hindustani.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "That is nice," he said more drowsily still, and she went on chanting and stroking, but when she looked at him again his black lashes were lying close against his cheeks, for his eyes were shut and he was fast asleep. So she got up softly, took her candle and crept away without making a sound.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: The moor was hidden in mist when the morning came, and the rain had not stopped pouring down. There could be no going out of doors. Martha was so busy that Mary had no opportunity of talking to her, but in the afternoon she asked her to come and sit with her in the nursery. She came bringing the stocking she was always knitting when she was doing nothing else.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "What's the matter with thee?" she asked as soon as they sat down. "Tha' looks as if tha'd somethin' to say."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I have. I have found out what the crying was," said Mary.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: Martha let her knitting drop on her knee and gazed at her with startled eyes.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I heard it in the night," Mary went on. "And I got up and went to see where it came from. It was Colin. I found him."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Eh! Miss Mary!" she said half crying. "Tha' shouldn't have done it - tha' shouldn't! Tha'll get me in trouble. I never told thee nothin' about him - but tha'll get me in trouble. I shall lose my place and what'll mother do!"
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "You won't lose your place," said Mary. "He was glad I came. We talked and talked and he said he was glad I came."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Was he?" cried Martha. "Art tha' sure? Tha' doesn't know what he's like when anything vexes him. He's a big lad to cry like a baby, but when he's in a passion he'll fair scream just to frighten us. He knows us daren't call our souls our own."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "He wasn't vexed," said Mary. "I asked him if I should go away and he made me stay. He asked me questions and I sat on a big footstool and talked to him about India and about the robin and gardens. He wouldn't let me go. He let me see his mother's picture. Before I left him I sang him to sleep."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I can scarcely believe thee!" she protested. "It's as if tha'd walked straight into a lion's den. If he'd been like he is most times he'd have throwed himself into one of his tantrums and roused th' house. He won't let strangers look at him."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "He let me look at him. I looked at him all the time and he looked at me. We stared!" said Mary.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I don't know what to do!" cried agitated Martha. "If Mrs. Medlock finds out, she'll think I broke orders and told thee and I shall be packed back to mother."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "He is not going to tell Mrs. Medlock anything about it yet. It's to be a sort of secret just at first," said Mary firmly. "And he says everybody is obliged to do as he pleases."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Aye, that's true enough - th' bad lad!" sighed Martha, wiping her forehead with her apron.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "He says Mrs. Medlock must. And he wants me to come and talk to him every day. And you are to tell me when he wants me."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Me!" said Martha; "I shall lose my place - I shall for sure!"
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "You can't if you are doing what he wants you to do and everybody is ordered to obey him," Mary argued.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Does tha' mean to say," cried Martha with wide open eyes, "that he was nice to thee!"
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Then tha' must have bewitched him!" decided Martha, drawing a long breath.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Do you mean Magic?" inquired Mary. "I've heard about Magic in India, but I can't make it. I just went into his room and I was so surprised to see him I stood and stared. And then he turned round and stared at me. And he thought I was a ghost or a dream and I thought perhaps he was. And it was so queer being there alone together in the middle of the night and not knowing about each other. And we began to ask each other questions. And when I asked him if I must go away he said I must not."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Th' world's comin' to a end!" gasped Martha.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Nobody knows for sure and certain," said Martha. "Mr. Craven went off his head like when he was born. Th' doctors thought he'd have to be put in a 'sylum. It was because Mrs. Craven died like I told you. He wouldn't set eyes on th' baby. He just raved and said it'd be another hunchback like him and it'd better die."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Is Colin a hunchback?" Mary asked. "He didn't look like one."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "He isn't yet," said Martha. "But he began all wrong. Mother said that there was enough trouble and raging in th' house to set any child wrong. They was afraid his back was weak an' they've always been takin' care of it - keepin' him lyin' down and not lettin' him walk. Once they made him wear a brace but he fretted so he was downright ill. Then a big doctor came to see him an' made them take it off. He talked to th' other doctor quite rough - in a polite way. He said there'd been too much medicine and too much lettin' him have his own way."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I think he's a very spoiled boy," said Mary.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Mother says there's no reason why any child should live that gets no fresh air an' doesn't do nothin' but lie on his back an' read picture-books an' take medicine. He's weak and hates th' trouble o' bein' taken out o' doors, an' he gets cold so easy he says it makes him ill."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I wonder," she said slowly, "if it would not do him good to go out into a garden and watch things growing. It did me good."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "One of th' worst fits he ever had," said Martha, "was one time they took him out where the roses is by the fountain. He'd been readin' in a paper about people gettin' somethin' he called 'rose cold' an' he began to sneeze an' said he'd got it an' then a new gardener as didn't know th' rules passed by an' looked at him curious. He threw himself into a passion an' he said he'd looked at him because he was going to be a hunchback. He cried himself into a fever an' was ill all night."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "If he ever gets angry at me, I'll never go and see him again," said Mary.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "He'll have thee if he wants thee," said Martha. "Tha' may as well know that at th' start."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: Very soon afterward a bell rang and she rolled up her knitting.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I dare say th' nurse wants me to stay with him a bit," she said. "I hope he's in a good temper."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: She was out of the room about ten minutes and then she came back with a puzzled expression.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Well, tha' has bewitched him," she said. "He's up on his sofa with his picture-books. He's told the nurse to stay away until six o'clock. I'm to wait in the next room. Th' minute she was gone he called me to him an' says, 'I want Mary Lennox to come and talk to me, and remember you're not to tell anyone.' You'd better go as quick as you can."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: Mary was quite willing to go quickly. She did not want to see Colin as much as she wanted to see Dickon; but she wanted to see him very much.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: There was a bright fire on the hearth when she entered his room, and in the daylight she saw it was a very beautiful room indeed. There were rich colors in the rugs and hangings and pictures and books on the walls which made it look glowing and comfortable even in spite of the gray sky and falling rain. Colin looked rather like a picture himself. He was wrapped in a velvet dressing-gown and sat against a big brocaded cushion. He had a red spot on each cheek.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Come in," he said. "I've been thinking about you all morning."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I've been thinking about you, too," answered Mary. "You don't know how frightened Martha is. She says Mrs. Medlock will think she told me about you and then she will be sent away."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Go and tell her to come here," he said. "She is in the next room."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: Mary went and brought her back. Poor Martha was shaking in her shoes. Colin was still frowning.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Have you to do what I please or have you not?" he demanded.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I have to do what you please, sir," Martha faltered, turning quite red.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Well, then, if I order you to bring Miss Mary to me, how can Medlock send you away if she finds it out?"
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I'll send her away if she dares to say a word about such a thing," said Master Craven grandly. "She wouldn't like that, I can tell you."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Thank you, sir," bobbing a curtsy, "I want to do my duty, sir."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "What I want is your duty" said Colin more grandly still. "I'll take care of you. Now go away."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: When the door closed behind Martha, Colin found Mistress Mary gazing at him as if he had set her wondering.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Why do you look at me like that?" he asked her. "What are you thinking about?"
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "This is the first one," said Mary, seating herself on the big stool. "Once in India I saw a boy who was a Rajah. He had rubies and emeralds and diamonds stuck all over him. He spoke to his people just as you spoke to Martha. Everybody had to do everything he told them - in a minute. I think they would have been killed if they hadn't."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I shall make you tell me about Rajahs presently," he said, "but first tell me what the second thing was."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I was thinking," said Mary, "how different you are from Dickon."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Who is Dickon?" he said. "What a queer name!"
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: She might as well tell him, she thought she could talk about Dickon without mentioning the secret garden. She had liked to hear Martha talk about him. Besides, she longed to talk about him. It would seem to bring him nearer.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "He is Martha's brother. He is twelve years old," she explained. "He is not like anyone else in the world. He can charm foxes and squirrels and birds just as the natives in India charm snakes. He plays a very soft tune on a pipe and they come and listen."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: There were some big books on a table at his side and he dragged one suddenly toward him.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "There is a picture of a snake-charmer in this," he exclaimed. "Come and look at it."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "He played on his pipe and they listened," Mary explained. "But he doesn't call it Magic. He says it's because he lives on the moor so much and he knows their ways. He says he feels sometimes as if he was a bird or a rabbit himself, he likes them so. I think he asked the robin questions. It seemed as if they talked to each other in soft chirps."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: Colin lay back on his cushion and his eyes grew larger and larger and the spots on his cheeks burned.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "He knows all about eggs and nests," Mary went on. "And he knows where foxes and badgers and otters live. He keeps them secret so that other boys won't find their holes and frighten them. He knows about everything that grows or lives on the moor."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Does he like the moor?" said Colin. "How can he when it's such a great, bare, dreary place?"
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "It's the most beautiful place," protested Mary. "Thousands of lovely things grow on it and there are thousands of little creatures all busy building nests and making holes and burrows and chippering or singing or squeaking to each other. They are so busy and having such fun under the earth or in the trees or heather. It's their world."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "How do you know all that?" said Colin, turning on his elbow to look at her.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I have never been there once, really," said Mary suddenly remembering. "I only drove over it in the dark. I thought it was hideous. Martha told me about it first and then Dickon.
