When Dickon talks about it you feel as if you saw things and heard them and as if you were standing in the heather with the sun shining and the gorse smelling like honey - and all full of bees and butterflies."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "You never see anything if you are ill," said Colin restlessly. He looked like a person listening to a new sound in the distance and wondering what it was.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "You can't if you stay in a room," said Mary.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I couldn't go on the moor," he said in a resentful tone.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: Mary was silent for a minute and then she said something bold.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Go on the moor! How could I? I am going to die."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "How do you know?" said Mary unsympathetically. She didn't like the way he had of talking about dying. She did not feel very sympathetic. She felt rather as if he almost boasted about it.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Oh, I've heard it ever since I remember," he answered crossly. "They are always whispering about it and thinking I don't notice. They wish I would, too."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: Mistress Mary felt quite contrary. She pinched her lips together.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "If they wished I would," she said, "I wouldn't. Who wishes you would?"
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "The servants - and of course Dr. Craven because he would get Misselthwaite and be rich instead of poor. He daren't say so, but he always looks cheerful when I am worse. When I had typhoid fever his face got quite fat. I think my father wishes it, too."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I don't believe he does," said Mary quite obstinately.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: And then he lay back on his cushion and was still, as if he were thinking. And there was quite a long silence. Perhaps they were both of them thinking strange things children do not usually think of.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I like the grand doctor from London, because he made them take the iron thing off," said Mary at last "Did he say you were going to die?"
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "He didn't whisper," Colin answered. "Perhaps he knew I hated whispering. I heard him say one thing quite aloud. He said, 'The lad might live if he would make up his mind to it. Put him in the humor.' It sounded as if he was in a temper."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I'll tell you who would put you in the humor, perhaps," said Mary reflecting. She felt as if she would like this thing to be settled one way or the other. "I believe Dickon would. He's always talking about live things. He never talks about dead things or things that are ill. He's always looking up in the sky to watch birds flying - or looking down at the earth to see something growing. He has such round blue eyes and they are so wide open with looking about. And he laughs such a big laugh with his wide mouth - and his cheeks are as red - as red as cherries."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: She pulled her stool nearer to the sofa and her expression quite changed at the remembrance of the wide curving mouth and wide open eyes.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "See here," she said. "Don't let us talk about dying; I don't like it. Let us talk about living. Let us talk and talk about Dickon. And then we will look at your pictures."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: They enjoyed themselves so much that they forgot the pictures and they forgot about the time. They had been laughing quite loudly over Ben Weatherstaff and his robin, and Colin was actually sitting up as if he had forgotten about his weak back, when he suddenly remembered something.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Do you know there is one thing we have never once thought of," he said. "We are cousins."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: It seemed so queer that they had talked so much and never remembered this simple thing that they laughed more than ever, because they had got into the humor to laugh at anything. And in the midst of the fun the door opened and in walked Dr. Craven and Mrs. Medlock.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: Dr. Craven started in actual alarm and Mrs. Medlock almost fell back because he had accidentally bumped against her.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Good Lord!" exclaimed poor Mrs. Medlock with her eyes almost starting out of her head. "Good Lord!"
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "What is this?" said Dr. Craven, coming forward. "What does it mean?"
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: Then Mary was reminded of the boy Rajah again. Colin answered as if neither the doctor's alarm nor Mrs. Medlock's terror were of the slightest consequence. He was as little disturbed or frightened as if an elderly cat and dog had walked into the room.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "This is my cousin, Mary Lennox," he said. "I asked her to come and talk to me. I like her. She must come and talk to me whenever I send for her."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: Dr. Craven turned reproachfully to Mrs. Medlock.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Oh, sir" she panted. "I don't know how it's happened. There's not a servant on the place tha'd dare to talk - they all have their orders."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Nobody told her anything," said Colin. "She heard me crying and found me herself. I am glad she came. Don't be silly, Medlock."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: Mary saw that Dr. Craven did not look pleased, but it was quite plain that he dare not oppose his patient. He sat down by Colin and felt his pulse.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I am afraid there has been too much excitement. Excitement is not good for you, my boy," he said.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I should be excited if she kept away," answered Colin, his eyes beginning to look dangerously sparkling. "I am better. She makes me better. The nurse must bring up her tea with mine. We will have tea together."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: Mrs. Medlock and Dr. Craven looked at each other in a troubled way, but there was evidently nothing to be done.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "He does look rather better, sir," ventured Mrs. Medlock. "But" - thinking the matter over - "he looked better this morning before she came into the room."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "She came into the room last night. She stayed with me a long time. She sang a Hindustani song to me and it made me go to sleep," said Colin. "I was better when I wakened up. I wanted my breakfast. I want my tea now. Tell nurse, Medlock."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: Dr. Craven did not stay very long. He talked to the nurse for a few minutes when she came into the room and said a few words of warning to Colin. He must not talk too much; he must not forget that he was ill; he must not forget that he was very easily tired. Mary thought that there seemed to be a number of uncomfortable things he was not to forget.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: Colin looked fretful and kept his strange black-lashed eyes fixed on Dr. Craven's face.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I want to forget it," he said at last. "She makes me forget it. That is why I want her."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: Dr. Craven did not look happy when he left the room. He gave a puzzled glance at the little girl sitting on the large stool. She had become a stiff, silent child again as soon as he entered and he could not see what the attraction was. The boy actually did look brighter, however - and he sighed rather heavily as he went down the corridor.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "They are always wanting me to eat things when I don't want to," said Colin, as the nurse brought in the tea and put it on the table by the sofa. "Now, if you'll eat I will. Those muffins look so nice and hot. Tell me about Rajahs."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: After another week of rain the high arch of blue sky appeared again and the sun which poured down was quite hot. Though there had been no chance to see either the secret garden or Dickon, Mistress Mary had enjoyed herself very much. The week had not seemed long. She had spent hours of every day with Colin in his room, talking about Rajahs or gardens or Dickon and the cottage on the moor. They had looked at the splendid books and pictures and sometimes Mary had read things to Colin, and sometimes he had read a little to her. When he was amused and interested she thought he scarcely looked like an invalid at all, except that his face was so colorless and he was always on the sofa.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "You are a sly young one to listen and get out of your bed to go following things up like you did that night," Mrs. Medlock said once. "But there's no saying it's not been a sort of blessing to the lot of us. He's not had a tantrum or a whining fit since you made friends. The nurse was just going to give up the case because she was so sick of him, but she says she doesn't mind staying now you've gone on duty with her," laughing a little.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Th' air from th' moor has done thee good already," she had said. "Tha'rt not nigh so yeller and tha'rt not nigh so scrawny. Even tha' hair doesn't slamp down on tha' head so flat. It's got some life in it so as it sticks out a bit."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "It's like me," said Mary. "It's growing stronger and fatter. I'm sure there's more of it."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "It looks it, for sure," said Martha, ruffling it up a little round her face. "Tha'rt not half so ugly when it's that way an' there's a bit o' red in tha' cheeks."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: If gardens and fresh air had been good for her perhaps they would be good for Colin. But then, if he hated people to look at him, perhaps he would not like to see Dickon.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Why does it make you angry when you are looked at?" she inquired one day.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I always hated it," he answered, "even when I was very little. Then when they took me to the seaside and I used to lie in my carriage everybody used to stare and ladies would stop and talk to my nurse and then they would begin to whisper and I knew then they were saying I shouldn't live to grow up. Then sometimes the ladies would pat my cheeks and say 'Poor child!' Once when a lady did that I screamed out loud and bit her hand. She was so frightened she ran away."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "She thought you had gone mad like a dog," said Mary, not at all admiringly.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I don't care what she thought," said Colin, frowning.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I wonder why you didn't scream and bite me when I came into your room?" said Mary. Then she began to smile slowly.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I thought you were a ghost or a dream," he said. "You can't bite a ghost or a dream, and if you scream they don't care."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Would you hate it if - if a boy looked at you?" Mary asked uncertainly.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: He lay back on his cushion and paused thoughtfully.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "There's one boy," he said quite slowly, as if he were thinking over every word, "there's one boy I believe I shouldn't mind. It's that boy who knows where the foxes live - Dickon."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "The birds don't and other animals," he said, still thinking it over, "perhaps that's why I shouldn't. He's a sort of animal charmer and I am a boy animal."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: Then he laughed and she laughed too; in fact it ended in their both laughing a great deal and finding the idea of a boy animal hiding in his hole very funny indeed.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: What Mary felt afterward was that she need not fear about Dickon.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: On that first morning when the sky was blue again Mary wakened very early. The sun was pouring in slanting rays through the blinds and there was something so joyous in the sight of it that she jumped out of bed and ran to the window. She drew up the blinds and opened the window itself and a great waft of fresh, scented air blew in upon her. The moor was blue and the whole world looked as if something Magic had happened to it. There were tender little fluting sounds here and there and everywhere, as if scores of birds were beginning to tune up for a concert. Mary put her hand out of the window and held it in the sun.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "It's warm - warm!" she said. "It will make the green points push up and up and up, and it will make the bulbs and roots work and struggle with all their might under the earth."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: She kneeled down and leaned out of the window as far as she could, breathing big breaths and sniffing the air until she laughed because she remembered what Dickon's mother had said about the end of his nose quivering like a rabbit's.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "It must be very early," she said. "The little clouds are all pink and I've never seen the sky look like this. No one is up. I don't even hear the stable boys."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: A sudden thought made her scramble to her feet.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I can't wait! I am going to see the garden!"
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "It is all different already," she said. "The grass is greener and things are sticking up everywhere and things are uncurling and green buds of leaves are showing. This afternoon I am sure Dickon will come."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: The long warm rain had done strange things to the herbaceous beds which bordered the walk by the lower wall. There were things sprouting and pushing out from the roots of clumps of plants and there were actually here and there glimpses of royal purple and yellow unfurling among the stems of crocuses. Six months before Mistress Mary would not have seen how the world was waking up, but now she missed nothing.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Oh, Dickon! Dickon!" she cried out. "How could you get here so early! How could you! The sun has only just got up!"
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: He got up himself, laughing and glowing, and tousled; his eyes like a bit of the sky.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Eh!" he said. "I was up long before him. How could I have stayed abed! Th' world's all fair begun again this mornin', it has. An' it's workin' an' hummin' an' scratchin' an' pipin' an' nest-buildin' an' breathin' out scents, till you've got to be out on it 'stead o' lyin' on your back. When th' sun did jump up, th' moor went mad for joy, an' I was in the midst of th' heather, an' I run like mad myself, shoutin' an' singin'. An' I come straight here. I couldn't have stayed away. Why, th' garden was lyin' here waitin'!"
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: Mary put her hands on her chest, panting, as if she had been running herself.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Oh, Dickon! Dickon!" she said. "I'm so happy I can scarcely breathe!"
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: Seeing him talking to a stranger, the little bushy-tailed animal rose from its place under the tree and came to him, and the rook, cawing once, flew down from its branch and settled quietly on his shoulder.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "This is th' little fox cub," he said, rubbing the little reddish animal's head. "It's named Captain. An' this here's Soot. Soot he flew across th' moor with me an' Captain he run same as if th' hounds had been after him. They both felt same as I did."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: Neither of the creatures looked as if he were the least afraid of Mary. When Dickon began to walk about, Soot stayed on his shoulder and Captain trotted quietly close to his side.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "See here!" said Dickon. "See how these has pushed up, an' these an' these! An' Eh! Look at these here!"
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: He threw himself upon his knees and Mary went down beside him. They had come upon a whole clump of crocuses burst into purple and orange and gold. Mary bent her face down and kissed and kissed them.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "You never kiss a person in that way," she said when she lifted her head. "Flowers are so different."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Eh!" he said, "I've kissed mother many a time that way when I come in from th' moor after a day's roamin' an' she stood there at th' door in th' sun, lookin' so glad an' comfortable."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: They ran from one part of the garden to another and found so many wonders that they were obliged to remind themselves that they must whisper or speak low. He showed her swelling leafbuds on rose branches which had seemed dead. He showed her ten thousand new green points pushing through the mould. They put their eager young noses close to the earth and sniffed its warmed springtime breathing; they dug and pulled and laughed low with rapture until Mistress Mary's hair was as tumbled as Dickon's and her cheeks were almost as poppy red as his.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: There was every joy on earth in the secret garden that morning, and in the midst of them came a delight more delightful than all, because it was more wonderful. Swiftly something flew across the wall and darted through the trees to a close grown corner, a little flare of red-breasted bird with something hanging from its beak. Dickon stood quite still and put his hand on Mary almost as if they had suddenly found themselves laughing in a church.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "We munnot stir," he whispered in broad Yorkshire. "We munnot scarce breathe. I knowed he was mate-huntin' when I seed him last. It's Ben Weatherstaff's robin. He's buildin' his nest. He'll stay here if us don't flight him."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: They settled down softly upon the grass and sat there without moving.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Us mustn't seem as if us was watchin' him too close," said Dickon. "He'd be out with us for good if he got th' notion us was interferin' now. He'll be a good bit different till all this is over. He's settin' up housekeepin'. He'll be shyer an' readier to take things ill. He's got no time for visitin' an' gossipin'. Us must keep still a bit an' try to look as if us was grass an' trees an' bushes. Then when he's got used to seein' us I'll chirp a bit an' he'll know us'll not be in his way."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: Mistress Mary was not at all sure that she knew, as Dickon seemed to, how to try to look like grass and trees and bushes. But he had said the queer thing as if it were the simplest and most natural thing in the world, and she felt it must be quite easy to him, and indeed she watched him for a few minutes carefully, wondering if it was possible for him to quietly turn green and put out branches and leaves. But he only sat wonderfully still, and when he spoke dropped his voice to such a softness that it was curious that she could hear him, but she could.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "It's part o' th' springtime, this nest-buildin' is," he said. "I warrant it's been goin' on in th' same way every year since th' world was begun. They've got their way o' thinkin' and doin' things an' a body had better not meddle. You can lose a friend in springtime easier than any other season if you're too curious."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "If we talk about him I can't help looking at him," Mary said as softly as possible. "We must talk of something else. There is something I want to tell you."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "He'll like it better if us talks o' somethin' else," said Dickon. "What is it tha's got to tell me?"
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Well - do you know about Colin?" she whispered.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I've seen him. I have been to talk to him every day this week. He wants me to come. He says I'm making him forget about being ill and dying," answered Mary.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: Dickon looked actually relieved as soon as the surprise died away from his round face.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I am glad o' that," he exclaimed. "I'm right down glad. It makes me easier. I knowed I must say nothin' about him an' I don't like havin' to hide things."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Don't you like hiding the garden?" said Mary.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "What did she say?" she asked, not at all afraid to hear.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Everybody as knowed about Mester Craven knowed there was a little lad as was like to be a cripple, an' they knowed Mester Craven didn't like him to be talked about. Folks is sorry for Mester Craven because Mrs. Craven was such a pretty young lady an' they was so fond of each other. Mrs. Medlock stops in our cottage whenever she goes to Thwaite an' she doesn't mind talkin' to mother before us children, because she knows us has been brought up to be trusty. How did tha' find out about him? Martha was in fine trouble th' last time she came home. She said tha'd heard him frettin' an' tha' was askin' questions an' she didn't know what to say."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: Mary told him her story about the midnight wuthering of the wind which had wakened her and about the faint far-off sounds of the complaining voice which had led her down the dark corridors with her candle and had ended with her opening of the door of the dimly lighted room with the carven four-posted bed in the corner. When she described the small ivory-white face and the strange black-rimmed eyes Dickon shook his head.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Them's just like his mother's eyes, only hers was always laughin', they say," he said. "They say as Mr. Craven can't bear to see him when he's awake an' it's because his eyes is so like his mother's an' yet looks so different in his miserable bit of a face."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Do you think he wants to die?" whispered Mary.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "No, but he wishes he'd never been born. Mother she says that's th' worst thing on earth for a child. Them as is not wanted scarce ever thrives. Mester Craven he'd buy anythin' as money could buy for th' poor lad but he'd like to forget as he's on earth. For one thing, he's afraid he'll look at him some day and find he's growed hunchback."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Colin's so afraid of it himself that he won't sit up," said Mary. "He says he's always thinking that if he should feel a lump coming he should go crazy and scream himself to death."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Eh! he oughtn't to lie there thinkin' things like that," said Dickon. "No lad could get well as thought them sort o' things."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: The fox was lying on the grass close by him, looking up to ask for a pat now and then, and Dickon bent down and rubbed his neck softly and thought a few minutes in silence. Presently he lifted his head and looked round the garden.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "When first we got in here," he said, "it seemed like everything was gray. Look round now and tell me if tha' doesn't see a difference."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Why!" she cried, "the gray wall is changing. It is as if a green mist were creeping over it. It's almost like a green gauze veil."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Aye," said Dickon. "An' it'll be greener and greener till th' gray's all gone. Can tha' guess what I was thinkin'?"
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I know it was something nice," said Mary eagerly. "I believe it was something about Colin."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I was thinkin' that if he was out here he wouldn't be watchin' for lumps to grow on his back; he'd be watchin' for buds to break on th' rose-bushes, an' he'd likely be healthier," explained Dickon. "I was wonderin' if us could ever get him in th' humor to come out here an' lie under th' trees in his carriage."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I've been wondering that myself. I've thought of it almost every time I've talked to him," said Mary. "I've wondered if he could keep a secret and I've wondered if we could bring him here without anyone seeing us. I thought perhaps you could push his carriage. The doctor said he must have fresh air and if he wants us to take him out no one dare disobey him. He won't go out for other people and perhaps they will be glad if he will go out with us. He could order the gardeners to keep away so they wouldn't find out."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: Dickon was thinking very hard as he scratched Captain's back.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "It'd be good for him, I'll warrant," he said. "Us'd not be thinkin' he'd better never been born. Us'd be just two children watchin' a garden grow, an' he'd be another. Two lads an' a little lass just lookin' on at th' springtime. I warrant it'd be better than doctor's stuff."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "He's been lying in his room so long and he's always been so afraid of his back that it has made him queer," said Mary. "He knows a good many things out of books but he doesn't know anything else. He says he has been too ill to notice things and he hates going out of doors and hates gardens and gardeners. But he likes to hear about this garden because it is a secret. I daren't tell him much but he said he wanted to see it."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Us'll have him out here sometime for sure," said Dickon. "I could push his carriage well enough. Has tha' noticed how th' robin an' his mate has been workin' while we've been sittin' here? Look at him perched on that branch wonderin' where it'd be best to put that twig he's got in his beak."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: He made one of his low whistling calls and the robin turned his head and looked at him inquiringly, still holding his twig. Dickon spoke to him as Ben Weatherstaff did, but Dickon's tone was one of friendly advice.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Wheres'ever tha' puts it," he said, "it'll be all right. Tha' knew how to build tha' nest before tha' came out o' th' egg. Get on with thee, lad. Tha'st got no time to lose."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Oh, I do like to hear you talk to him!" Mary said, laughing delightedly. "Ben Weatherstaff scolds him and makes fun of him, and he hops about and looks as if he understood every word, and I know he likes it. Ben Weatherstaff says he is so conceited he would rather have stones thrown at him than not be noticed."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Tha' knows us won't trouble thee," he said to the robin. "Us is near bein' wild things ourselves. Us is nest-buildin' too, bless thee. Look out tha' doesn't tell on us."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: And though the robin did not answer, because his beak was occupied, Mary knew that when he flew away with his twig to his own corner of the garden the darkness of his dew-bright eye meant that he would not tell their secret for the world.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: They found a great deal to do that morning and Mary was late in returning to the house and was also in such a hurry to get back to her work that she quite forgot Colin until the last moment.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Tell Colin that I can't come and see him yet," she said to Martha. "I'm very busy in the garden."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Eh! Miss Mary," she said, "it may put him all out of humor when I tell him that."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: But Mary was not as afraid of him as other people were and she was not a self-sacrificing person.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I can't stay," she answered. "Dickon's waiting for me;" and she ran away.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: The afternoon was even lovelier and busier than the morning had been. Already nearly all the weeds were cleared out of the garden and most of the roses and trees had been pruned or dug about. Dickon had brought a spade of his own and he had taught Mary to use all her tools, so that by this time it was plain that though the lovely wild place was not likely to become a "gardener's garden" it would be a wilderness of growing things before the springtime was over.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "There'll be apple blossoms an' cherry blossoms overhead," Dickon said, working away with all his might. "An' there'll be peach an' plum trees in bloom against th' walls, an' th' grass'll be a carpet o' flowers."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Tha's a good bit stronger than tha' was," Dickon said, looking at her as she was digging. "Tha's beginning to look different, for sure."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: Mary was glowing with exercise and good spirits.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I'm getting fatter and fatter every day," she said quite exultantly. "Mrs. Medlock will have to get me some bigger dresses. Martha says my hair is growing thicker. It isn't so flat and stringy."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: The sun was beginning to set and sending deep gold-colored rays slanting under the trees when they parted.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "It'll be fine tomorrow," said Dickon. "I'll be at work by sunrise."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: She ran back to the house as quickly as her feet would carry her. She wanted to tell Colin about Dickon's fox cub and the rook and about what the springtime had been doing. She felt sure he would like to hear. So it was not very pleasant when she opened the door of her room, to see Martha standing waiting for her with a doleful face.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "What is the matter?" she asked. "What did Colin say when you told him I couldn't come?"
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Eh!" said Martha, "I wish tha'd gone. He was nigh goin' into one o' his tantrums. There's been a nice to do all afternoon to keep him quiet. He would watch the clock all th' time."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: Mary's lips pinched themselves together. She was no more used to considering other people than Colin was and she saw no reason why an ill-tempered boy should interfere with the thing she liked best. She knew nothing about the pitifulness of people who had been ill and nervous and who did not know that they could control their tempers and need not make other people ill and nervous, too. When she had had a headache in India she had done her best to see that everybody else also had a headache or something quite as bad. And she felt she was quite right; but of course now she felt that Colin was quite wrong.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: He was not on his sofa when she went into his room. He was lying flat on his back in bed and he did not turn his head toward her as she came in. This was a bad beginning and Mary marched up to him with her stiff manner.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I did get up this morning when I thought you were coming," he answered, without looking at her. "I made them put me back in bed this afternoon. My back ached and my head ached and I was tired. Why didn't you come?"
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I was working in the garden with Dickon," said Mary.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: Colin frowned and condescended to look at her.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I won't let that boy come here if you go and stay with him instead of coming to talk to me," he said.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: Mary flew into a fine passion. She could fly into a passion without making a noise. She just grew sour and obstinate and did not care what happened.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "If you send Dickon away, I'll never come into this room again!" she retorted.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I'll make you," said Colin. "They shall drag you in."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Shall they, Mr. Rajah!" said Mary fiercely. "They may drag me in but they can't make me talk when they get me here. I'll sit and clench my teeth and never tell you one thing. I won't even look at you. I'll stare at the floor!"
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: They were a nice agreeable pair as they glared at each other. If they had been two little street boys they would have sprung at each other and had a rough-and-tumble fight. As it was, they did the next thing to it.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "What are you?" said Mary. "Selfish people always say that. Anyone is selfish who doesn't do what they want. You're more selfish than I am. You're the most selfish boy I ever saw."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I'm not!" snapped Colin. "I'm not as selfish as your fine Dickon is! He keeps you playing in the dirt when he knows I am all by myself. He's selfish, if you like!"
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "He's nicer than any other boy that ever lived!" she said. "He's - he's like an angel!" It might sound rather silly to say that but she did not care.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "A nice angel!" Colin sneered ferociously. "He's a common cottage boy off the moor!"
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "He's better than a common Rajah!" retorted Mary. "He's a thousand times better!"
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: Because she was the stronger of the two she was beginning to get the better of him. The truth was that he had never had a fight with anyone like himself in his life and, upon the whole, it was rather good for him, though neither he nor Mary knew anything about that. He turned his head on his pillow and shut his eyes and a big tear was squeezed out and ran down his cheek. He was beginning to feel pathetic and sorry for himself - not for anyone else.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I'm not as selfish as you, because I'm always ill, and I'm sure there is a lump coming on my back," he said. "And I am going to die besides."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "You're not!" contradicted Mary unsympathetically.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: He opened his eyes quite wide with indignation. He had never heard such a thing said before. He was at once furious and slightly pleased, if a person could be both at one time.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I'm not?" he cried. "I am! You know I am! Everybody says so."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I don't believe it!" said Mary sourly. "You just say that to make people sorry. I believe you're proud of it. I don't believe it! If you were a nice boy it might be true - but you're too nasty!"
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: In spite of his invalid back Colin sat up in bed in quite a healthy rage.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Get out of the room!" he shouted and he caught hold of his pillow and threw it at her. He was not strong enough to throw it far and it only fell at her feet, but Mary's face looked as pinched as a nutcracker.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I'm going," she said. "And I won't come back!"
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: She walked to the door and when she reached it she turned round and spoke again.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I was going to tell you all sorts of nice things," she said. "Dickon brought his fox and his rook and I was going to tell you all about them. Now I won't tell you a single thing!"
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: She marched out of the door and closed it behind her, and there to her great astonishment she found the trained nurse standing as if she had been listening and, more amazing still - she was laughing. She was a big handsome young woman who ought not to have been a trained nurse at all, as she could not bear invalids and she was always making excuses to leave Colin to Martha or anyone else who would take her place. Mary had never liked her, and she simply stood and gazed up at her as she stood giggling into her handkerchief..
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "At you two young ones," said the nurse. "It's the best thing that could happen to the sickly pampered thing to have someone to stand up to him that's as spoiled as himself;" and she laughed into her handkerchief again. "If he'd had a young vixen of a sister to fight with it would have been the saving of him."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I don't know and I don't care," said the nurse. "Hysterics and temper are half what ails him."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "You'll find out if you work him into a tantrum after this - but at any rate you've given him something to have hysterics about, and I'm glad of it."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: Martha was waiting for her and the trouble in her face had been temporarily replaced by interest and curiosity. There was a wooden box on the table and its cover had been removed and revealed that it was full of neat packages.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Mr. Craven sent it to you," said Martha. "It looks as if it had picture-books in it."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: Mary remembered what he had asked her the day she had gone to his room. "Do you want anything - dolls - toys - books?" She opened the package wondering if he had sent a doll, and also wondering what she should do with it if he had. But he had not sent one. There were several beautiful books such as Colin had, and two of them were about gardens and were full of pictures. There were two or three games and there was a beautiful little writing-case with a gold monogram on it and a gold pen and inkstand.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: Everything was so nice that her pleasure began to crowd her anger out of her mind. She had not expected him to remember her at all and her hard little heart grew quite warm.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I can write better than I can print," she said, "and the first thing I shall write with that pen will be a letter to tell him I am much obliged."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "He always began to think about it when he was cross or tired," she said to herself. "And he has been cross today. Perhaps - perhaps he has been thinking about it all afternoon."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: She stood still, looking down at the carpet and thinking.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I said I would never go back again - " she hesitated, knitting her brows - "but perhaps, just perhaps, I will go and see - if he wants me - in the morning. Perhaps he'll try to throw his pillow at me again, but - I think - I'll go."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I'll go out before breakfast and work with Dickon and then afterward - I believe - I'll go to see him."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: She thought it was the middle of the night when she was awakened by such dreadful sounds that she jumped out of bed in an instant. What was it - what was it? The next minute she felt quite sure she knew. Doors were opened and shut and there were hurrying feet in the corridors and someone was crying and screaming at the same time, screaming and crying in a horrible way.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "It's Colin," she said. "He's having one of those tantrums the nurse called hysterics. How awful it sounds."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: As she listened to the sobbing screams she did not wonder that people were so frightened that they gave him his own way in everything rather than hear them. She put her hands over her ears and felt sick and shivering.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I don't know what to do. I don't know what to do," she kept saying. "I can't bear it."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: Once she wondered if he would stop if she dared go to him and then she remembered how he had driven her out of the room and thought that perhaps the sight of her might make him worse. Even when she pressed her hands more tightly over her ears she could not keep the awful sounds out. She hated them so and was so terrified by them that suddenly they began to make her angry and she felt as if she should like to fly into a tantrum herself and frighten him as he was frightening her. She was not used to anyone's tempers but her own. She took her hands from her ears and sprang up and stamped her foot.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "He ought to be stopped! Somebody ought to make him stop! Somebody ought to beat him!" she cried out.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: Just then she heard feet almost running down the corridor and her door opened and the nurse came in. She was not laughing now by any means. She even looked rather pale.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "He's worked himself into hysterics," she said in a great hurry. "He'll do himself harm. No one can do anything with him. You come and try, like a good child. He likes you."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "He turned me out of the room this morning," said Mary, stamping her foot with excitement.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: The stamp rather pleased the nurse. The truth was that she had been afraid she might find Mary crying and hiding her head under the bed-clothes.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "That's right," she said. "You're in the right humor. You go and scold him. Give him something new to think of. Do go, child, as quick as ever you can."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: It was not until afterward that Mary realized that the thing had been funny as well as dreadful - that it was funny that all the grown-up people were so frightened that they came to a little girl just because they guessed she was almost as bad as Colin himself.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: She flew along the corridor and the nearer she got to the screams the higher her temper mounted. She felt quite wicked by the time she reached the door. She slapped it open with her hand and ran across the room to the four-posted bed.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "You stop!" she almost shouted. "You stop! I hate you! Everybody hates you! I wish everybody would run out of the house and let you scream yourself to death! You will scream yourself to death in a minute, and I wish you would!"
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: A nice sympathetic child could neither have thought nor said such things, but it just happened that the shock of hearing them was the best possible thing for this hysterical boy whom no one had ever dared to restrain or contradict.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "If you scream another scream," she said, "I'll scream too - and I can scream louder than you can and I'll frighten you, I'll frighten you!"
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: He actually had stopped screaming because she had startled him so. The scream which had been coming almost choked him. The tears were streaming down his face and he shook all over.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I can't stop!" he gasped and sobbed. "I can't - I can't!"
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "You can!" shouted Mary. "Half that ails you is hysterics and temper - just hysterics - hysterics - hysterics!" and she stamped each time she said it.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I felt the lump - I felt it," choked out Colin. "I knew I should. I shall have a hunch on my back and then I shall die," and he began to writhe again and turned on his face and sobbed and wailed but he didn't scream.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "You didn't feel a lump!" contradicted Mary fiercely. "If you did it was only a hysterical lump. Hysterics makes lumps. There's nothing the matter with your horrid back - nothing but hysterics! Turn over and let me look at it!"
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: She liked the word "hysterics" and felt somehow as if it had an effect on him. He was probably like herself and had never heard it before.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Nurse," she commanded, "come here and show me his back this minute!"
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: The nurse, Mrs. Medlock and Martha had been standing huddled together near the door staring at her, their mouths half open. All three had gasped with fright more than once. The nurse came forward as if she were half afraid. Colin was heaving with great breathless sobs.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Perhaps he - he won't let me," she hesitated in a low voice.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "There's not a single lump there!" she said at last. "There's not a lump as big as a pin - except backbone lumps, and you can only feel them because you're thin. I've got backbone lumps myself, and they used to stick out as much as yours do, until I began to get fatter, and I am not fat enough yet to hide them. There's not a lump as big as a pin! If you ever say there is again, I shall laugh!"
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I didn't know," ventured the nurse, "that he thought he had a lump on his spine. His back is weak because he won't try to sit up. I could have told him there was no lump there." Colin gulped and turned his face a little to look at her.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: Colin turned on his face again and but for his long-drawn broken breaths, which were the dying down of his storm of sobbing, he lay still for a minute, though great tears streamed down his face and wet the pillow. Actually the tears meant that a curious great relief had come to him. Presently he turned and looked at the nurse again and strangely enough he was not like a Rajah at all as he spoke to her.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Do you think - I could - live to grow up?" he said.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: The nurse was neither clever nor soft-hearted but she could repeat some of the London doctor's words.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "You probably will if you will do what you are told to do and not give way to your temper, and stay out a great deal in the fresh air."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: Colin's tantrum had passed and he was weak and worn out with crying and this perhaps made him feel gentle. He put out his hand a little toward Mary, and I am glad to say that, her own tantum having passed, she was softened too and met him half-way with her hand, so that it was a sort of making up.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I'll - I'll go out with you, Mary," he said. "I shan't hate fresh air if we can find - " He remembered just in time to stop himself from saying "if we can find the secret garden" and he ended, "I shall like to go out with you if Dickon will come and push my chair. I do so want to see Dickon and the fox and the crow."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: The nurse remade the tumbled bed and shook and straightened the pillows. Then she made Colin a cup of beef tea and gave a cup to Mary, who really was very glad to get it after her excitement. Mrs. Medlock and Martha gladly slipped away, and after everything was neat and calm and in order the nurse looked as if she would very gladly slip away also. She was a healthy young woman who resented being robbed of her sleep and she yawned quite openly as she looked at Mary, who had pushed her big footstool close to the four-posted bed and was holding Colin's hand.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "You must go back and get your sleep out," she said. "He'll drop off after a while - if he's not too upset. Then I'll lie down myself in the next room."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Would you like me to sing you that song I learned from my Ayah?" Mary whispered to Colin.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: His hand pulled hers gently and he turned his tired eyes on her appealingly.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Oh, yes!" he answered. "It's such a soft song. I shall go to sleep in a minute."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I will put him to sleep," Mary said to the yawning nurse. "You can go if you like."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Well," said the nurse, with an attempt at reluctance. "If he doesn't go to sleep in half an hour you must call me."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: The nurse was out of the room in a minute and as soon as she was gone Colin pulled Mary's hand again.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I almost told," he said; "but I stopped myself in time. I won't talk and I'll go to sleep, but you said you had a whole lot of nice things to tell me. Have you - do you think you have found out anything at all about the way into the secret garden?"
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: Mary looked at his poor little tired face and swollen eyes and her heart relented.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Ye-es," she answered, "I think I have. And if you will go to sleep I will tell you tomorrow." His hand quite trembled.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Oh, Mary!" he said. "Oh, Mary! If I could get into it I think I should live to grow up! Do you suppose that instead of singing the Ayah song - you could just tell me softly as you did that first day what you imagine it looks like inside? I am sure it will make me go to sleep."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: He closed his eyes and lay quite still and she held his hand and began to speak very slowly and in a very low voice.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: The soft drone of her voice was making him stiller and stiller and she saw it and went on.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Perhaps they are coming up through the grass - perhaps there are clusters of purple crocuses and gold ones - even now. Perhaps the leaves are beginning to break out and uncurl - and perhaps - the gray is changing and a green gauze veil is creeping - and creeping over - everything. And the birds are coming to look at it - because it is - so safe and still. And perhaps - perhaps - perhaps - " very softly and slowly indeed, "the robin has found a mate - and is building a nest."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: Of course Mary did not waken early the next morning. She slept late because she was tired, and when Martha brought her breakfast she told her that though Colin was quite quiet he was ill and feverish as he always was after he had worn himself out with a fit of crying. Mary ate her breakfast slowly as she listened.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "He says he wishes tha' would please go and see him as soon as tha' can," Martha said. "It's queer what a fancy he's took to thee. Tha' did give it him last night for sure - didn't tha? Nobody else would have dared to do it. Eh! poor lad! He's been spoiled till salt won't save him. Mother says as th' two worst things as can happen to a child is never to have his own way - or always to have it. She doesn't know which is th' worst. Tha' was in a fine temper tha'self, too. But he says to me when I went into his room, 'Please ask Miss Mary if she'll please come an' talk to me?' Think o' him saying please! Will you go, Miss?"
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I'll run and see Dickon first," said Mary. "No, I'll go and see Colin first and tell him - I know what I'll tell him," with a sudden inspiration.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: She had her hat on when she appeared in Colin's room and for a second he looked disappointed. He was in bed. His face was pitifully white and there were dark circles round his eyes.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I'm glad you came," he said. "My head aches and I ache all over because I'm so tired. Are you going somewhere?"
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I won't be long," she said. "I'm going to Dickon, but I'll come back. Colin, it's - it's something about the garden."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: His whole face brightened and a little color came into it.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Oh! is it?" he cried out. "I dreamed about it all night. I heard you say something about gray changing into green, and I dreamed I was standing in a place all filled with trembling little green leaves - and there were birds on nests everywhere and they looked so soft and still. I'll lie and think about it until you come back."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: In five minutes Mary was with Dickon in their garden. The fox and the crow were with him again and this time he had brought two tame squirrels.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I came over on the pony this mornin'," he said. "Eh! he is a good little chap - Jump is! I brought these two in my pockets. This here one he's called Nut an' this here other one's called Shell."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: When he said "Nut" one squirrel leaped on to his right shoulder and when he said "Shell" the other one leaped on to his left shoulder.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: When they sat down on the grass with Captain curled at their feet, Soot solemnly listening on a tree and Nut and Shell nosing about close to them, it seemed to Mary that it would be scarcely bearable to leave such delightfulness, but when she began to tell her story somehow the look in Dickon's funny face gradually changed her mind. She could see he felt sorrier for Colin than she did. He looked up at the sky and all about him.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Just listen to them birds - th' world seems full of 'em - all whistlin' an' pipin'," he said. "Look at 'em dartin' about, an' hearken at 'em callin' to each other. Come springtime seems like as if all th' world's callin'. The leaves is uncurlin' so you can see 'em - an', my word, th' nice smells there is about!" sniffing with his happy turned-up nose. "An' that poor lad lyin' shut up an' seein' so little that he gets to thinkin' o' things as sets him screamin'. Eh! my! we mun get him out here - we mun get him watchin' an listenin' an' sniffin' up th' air an' get him just soaked through wi' sunshine. An' we munnot lose no time about it."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: When he was very much interested he often spoke quite broad Yorkshire though at other times he tried to modify his dialect so that Mary could better understand. But she loved his broad Yorkshire and had in fact been trying to learn to speak it herself. So she spoke a little now.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Aye, that we mun," she said (which meant "Yes, indeed, we must"). "I'll tell thee what us'll do first," she proceeded, and Dickon grinned, because when the little wench tried to twist her tongue into speaking Yorkshire it amused him very much. "He's took a graidely fancy to thee. He wants to see thee and he wants to see Soot an' Captain. When I go back to the house to talk to him I'll ax him if tha' canna' come an' see him tomorrow mornin' - an' bring tha' creatures wi' thee - an' then - in a bit, when there's more leaves out, an' happen a bud or two, we'll get him to come out an' tha' shall push him in his chair an' we'll bring him here an' show him everything."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: When she stopped she was quite proud of herself. She had never made a long speech in Yorkshire before and she had remembered very well.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Tha' mun talk a bit o' Yorkshire like that to Mester Colin," Dickon chuckled. "Tha'll make him laugh an' there's nowt as good for ill folk as laughin' is. Mother says she believes as half a hour's good laugh every mornin' 'ud cure a chap as was makin' ready for typhus fever."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I'm going to talk Yorkshire to him this very day," said Mary, chuckling herself.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: The garden had reached the time when every day and every night it seemed as if Magicians were passing through it drawing loveliness out of the earth and the boughs with wands. It was hard to go away and leave it all, particularly as Nut had actually crept on to her dress and Shell had scrambled down the trunk of the apple-tree they sat under and stayed there looking at her with inquiring eyes. But she went back to the house and when she sat down close to Colin's bed he began to sniff as Dickon did though not in such an experienced way.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "You smell like flowers and - and fresh things," he cried out quite joyously. "What is it you smell of? It's cool and warm and sweet all at the same time."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "It's th' wind from th' moor," said Mary. "It comes o' sittin' on th' grass under a tree wi' Dickon an' wi' Captain an' Soot an' Nut an' Shell. It's th' springtime an' out o' doors an' sunshine as smells so graidely."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: She said it as broadly as she could, and you do not know how broadly Yorkshire sounds until you have heard someone speak it. Colin began to laugh.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "What are you doing?" he said. "I never heard you talk like that before. How funny it sounds."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I'm givin' thee a bit o' Yorkshire," answered Mary triumphantly. "I canna' talk as graidely as Dickon an' Martha can but tha' sees I can shape a bit. Doesn't tha' understand a bit o' Yorkshire when tha' hears it? An' tha' a Yorkshire lad thysel' bred an' born! Eh! I wonder tha'rt not ashamed o' thy face."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: And then she began to laugh too and they both laughed until they could not stop themselves and they laughed until the room echoed and Mrs. Medlock opening the door to come in drew back into the corridor and stood listening amazed.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Well, upon my word!" she said, speaking rather broad Yorkshire herself because there was no one to hear her and she was so astonished. "Whoever heard th' like! Whoever on earth would ha' thought it!"
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Does he really understand everything Dickon says?" Colin asked.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "It seems as if he does," answered Mary. "Dickon says anything will understand if you're friends with it for sure, but you have to be friends for sure."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: Colin lay quiet a little while and his strange gray eyes seemed to be staring at the wall, but Mary saw he was thinking.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I wish I was friends with things," he said at last, "but I'm not. I never had anything to be friends with, and I can't bear people."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Yes, I can," he answered. "It's funny but I even like you."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Ben Weatherstaff said I was like him," said Mary. "He said he'd warrant we'd both got the same nasty tempers. I think you are like him too. We are all three alike - you and I and Ben Weatherstaff. He said we were neither of us much to look at and we were as sour as we looked. But I don't feel as sour as I used to before I knew the robin and Dickon."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Yes," answered Mary without any affectation. "I should have detested you if I had seen you before I saw the robin and Dickon."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Mary," he said, "I wish I hadn't said what I did about sending Dickon away. I hated you when you said he was like an angel and I laughed at you but - but perhaps he is."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Well, it was rather funny to say it," she admitted frankly, "because his nose does turn up and he has a big mouth and his clothes have patches all over them and he talks broad Yorkshire, but - but if an angel did come to Yorkshire and live on the moor - if there was a Yorkshire angel - I believe he'd understand the green things and know how to make them grow and he would know how to talk to the wild creatures as Dickon does and they'd know he was friends for sure."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I shouldn't mind Dickon looking at me," said Colin; "I want to see him."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: Quite suddenly it came into her mind that this was the minute to tell him. Colin knew something new was coming.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: Mary was so anxious that she got up from her stool and came to him and caught hold of both his hands.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Can I trust you? I trusted Dickon because birds trusted him. Can I trust you - for sure - for sure?" she implored.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: Her face was so solemn that he almost whispered his answer.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Well, Dickon will come to see you tomorrow morning, and he'll bring his creatures with him."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "But that's not all," Mary went on, almost pale with solemn excitement. "The rest is better. There is a door into the garden. I found it. It is under the ivy on the wall."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: If he had been a strong healthy boy Colin would probably have shouted "Hooray! Hooray! Hooray!" but he was weak and rather hysterical; his eyes grew bigger and bigger and he gasped for breath.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Oh! Mary!" he cried out with a half sob. "Shall I see it? Shall I get into it? Shall I live to get into it?" and he clutched her hands and dragged her toward him.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Of course you'll see it!" snapped Mary indignantly. "Of course you'll live to get into it! Don't be silly!"
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: And she was so un-hysterical and natural and childish that she brought him to his senses and he began to laugh at himself and a few minutes afterward she was sitting on her stool again telling him not what she imagined the secret garden to be like but what it really was, and Colin's aches and tiredness were forgotten and he was listening enraptured.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "It is just what you thought it would be," he said at last. "It sounds just as if you had really seen it. You know I said that when you told me first."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: Mary hesitated about two minutes and then boldly spoke the truth.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I had seen it - and I had been in," she said. "I found the key and got in weeks ago. But I daren't tell you - I daren't because I was so afraid I couldn't trust you - for sure!"
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: Of course Dr. Craven had been sent for the morning after Colin had had his tantrum. He was always sent for at once when such a thing occurred and he always found, when he arrived, a white shaken boy lying on his bed, sulky and still so hysterical that he was ready to break into fresh sobbing at the least word. In fact, Dr. Craven dreaded and detested the difficulties of these visits. On this occasion he was away from Misselthwaite Manor until afternoon.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "How is he?" he asked Mrs. Medlock rather irritably when he arrived. "He will break a blood-vessel in one of those fits some day. The boy is half insane with hysteria and self-indulgence."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Well, sir," answered Mrs. Medlock, "you'll scarcely believe your eyes when you see him. That plain sour-faced child that's almost as bad as himself has just bewitched him. How she's done it there's no telling. The Lord knows she's nothing to look at and you scarcely ever hear her speak, but she did what none of us dare do. She just flew at him like a little cat last night, and stamped her feet and ordered him to stop screaming, and somehow she startled him so that he actually did stop, and this afternoon - well just come up and see, sir. It's past crediting."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: The scene which Dr. Craven beheld when he entered his patient's room was indeed rather astonishing to him. As Mrs. Medlock opened the door he heard laughing and chattering. Colin was on his sofa in his dressing-gown and he was sitting up quite straight looking at a picture in one of the garden books and talking to the plain child who at that moment could scarcely be called plain at all because her face was so glowing with enjoyment.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Those long spires of blue ones - we'll have a lot of those," Colin was announcing. "They're called Del-phin-iums."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Dickon says they're larkspurs made big and grand," cried Mistress Mary. "There are clumps there already."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: Then they saw Dr. Craven and stopped. Mary became quite still and Colin looked fretful.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I am sorry to hear you were ill last night, my boy," Dr. Craven said a trifle nervously. He was rather a nervous man.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I'm better now - much better," Colin answered, rather like a Rajah. "I'm going out in my chair in a day or two if it is fine. I want some fresh air."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: Dr. Craven sat down by him and felt his pulse and looked at him curiously.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "It must be a very fine day," he said, "and you must be very careful not to tire yourself."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Fresh air won't tire me," said the young Rajah.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: As there had been occasions when this same young gentleman had shrieked aloud with rage and had insisted that fresh air would give him cold and kill him, it is not to be wondered at that his doctor felt somewhat startled.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I thought you did not like fresh air," he said.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I don't when I am by myself," replied the Rajah; "but my cousin is going out with me."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "And the nurse, of course?" suggested Dr. Craven.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "No, I will not have the nurse," so magnificently that Mary could not help remembering how the young native Prince had looked with his diamonds and emeralds and pearls stuck all over him and the great rubies on the small dark hand he had waved to command his servants to approach with salaams and receive his orders.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "My cousin knows how to take care of me. I am always better when she is with me. She made me better last night. A very strong boy I know will push my carriage."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: Dr. Craven felt rather alarmed. If this tiresome hysterical boy should chance to get well he himself would lose all chance of inheriting Misselthwaite; but he was not an unscrupulous man, though he was a weak one, and he did not intend to let him run into actual danger.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "He must be a strong boy and a steady boy," he said. "And I must know something about him. Who is he? What is his name?"
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "It's Dickon," Mary spoke up suddenly. She felt somehow that everybody who knew the moor must know Dickon. And she was right, too. She saw that in a moment Dr. Craven's serious face relaxed into a relieved smile.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Oh, Dickon," he said. "If it is Dickon you will be safe enough. He's as strong as a moor pony, is Dickon."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "And he's trusty," said Mary. "He's th' trustiest lad i' Yorkshire." She had been talking Yorkshire to Colin and she forgot herself.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Did Dickon teach you that?" asked Dr. Craven, laughing outright.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I'm learning it as if it was French," said Mary rather coldly. "It's like a native dialect in India. Very clever people try to learn them. I like it and so does Colin."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Well, well," he said. "If it amuses you perhaps it won't do you any harm. Did you take your bromide last night, Colin?"
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "No," Colin answered. "I wouldn't take it at first and after Mary made me quiet she talked me to sleep - in a low voice - about the spring creeping into a garden."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I don't want to remember," interrupted the Rajah, appearing again. "When I lie by myself and remember I begin to have pains everywhere and I think of things that make me begin to scream because I hate them so. If there was a doctor anywhere who could make you forget you were ill instead of remembering it I would have him brought here." And he waved a thin hand which ought really to have been covered with royal signet rings made of rubies. "It is because my cousin makes me forget that she makes me better."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: Dr. Craven had never made such a short stay after a "tantrum"; usually he was obliged to remain a very long time and do a great many things. This afternoon he did not give any medicine or leave any new orders and he was spared any disagreeable scenes. When he went downstairs he looked very thoughtful and when he talked to Mrs. Medlock in the library she felt that he was a much puzzled man.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Well, sir," she ventured, "could you have believed it?"
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "It is certainly a new state of affairs," said the doctor. "And there's no denying it is better than the old one."
