quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I believe Susan Sowerby's right - I do that," said Mrs. Medlock. "I stopped in her cottage on my way to Thwaite yesterday and had a bit of talk with her. And she says to me, 'Well, Sarah Ann, she mayn't be a good child, an' she mayn't be a pretty one, but she's a child, an' children needs children.' We went to school together, Susan Sowerby and me."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "She's the best sick nurse I know," said Dr. Craven. "When I find her in a cottage I know the chances are that I shall save my patient."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: Mrs. Medlock smiled. She was fond of Susan Sowerby.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "She's a shrewd woman," said Dr. Craven, putting on his coat.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "You've been out! You've been out! There's that nice smell of leaves!" he cried.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: She had been running and her hair was loose and blown and she was bright with the air and pink-cheeked, though he could not see it.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "It's so beautiful!" she said, a little breathless with her speed. "You never saw anything so beautiful! It has come! I thought it had come that other morning, but it was only coming. It is here now! It has come, the Spring! Dickon says so!"
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Has it?" cried Colin, and though he really knew nothing about it he felt his heart beat. He actually sat up in bed.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Open the window!" he added, laughing half with joyful excitement and half at his own fancy. "Perhaps we may hear golden trumpets!"
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: And though he laughed, Mary was at the window in a moment and in a moment more it was opened wide and freshness and softness and scents and birds' songs were pouring through.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "That's fresh air," she said. "Lie on your back and draw in long breaths of it. That's what Dickon does when he's lying on the moor. He says he feels it in his veins and it makes him strong and he feels as if he could live forever and ever. Breathe it and breathe it."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: She was only repeating what Dickon had told her, but she caught Colin's fancy.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Things are crowding up out of the earth," she ran on in a hurry. "And there are flowers uncurling and buds on everything and the green veil has covered nearly all the gray and the birds are in such a hurry about their nests for fear they may be too late that some of them are even fighting for places in the secret garden. And the rose-bushes look as wick as wick can be, and there are primroses in the lanes and woods, and the seeds we planted are up, and Dickon has brought the fox and the crow and the squirrels and a new-born lamb."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: She was describing it with great joy and Colin was listening and drawing in long breaths of air when the nurse entered. She started a little at the sight of the open window. She had sat stifling in the room many a warm day because her patient was sure that open windows gave people cold.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Are you sure you are not chilly, Master Colin?" she inquired.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "No," was the answer. "I am breathing long breaths of fresh air. It makes you strong. I am going to get up to the sofa for breakfast. My cousin will have breakfast with me."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: The nurse went away, concealing a smile, to give the order for two breakfasts. She found the servants' hall a more amusing place than the invalid's chamber and just now everybody wanted to hear the news from upstairs. There was a great deal of joking about the unpopular young recluse who, as the cook said, "had found his master, and good for him." The servants' hall had been very tired of the tantrums, and the butler, who was a man with a family, had more than once expressed his opinion that the invalid would be all the better "for a good hiding."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: When Colin was on his sofa and the breakfast for two was put upon the table he made an announcement to the nurse in his most Rajah-like manner.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "A boy, and a fox, and a crow, and two squirrels, and a new-born lamb, are coming to see me this morning. I want them brought upstairs as soon as they come," he said. "You are not to begin playing with the animals in the servants' hall and keep them there. I want them here."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: The nurse gave a slight gasp and tried to conceal it with a cough.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I'll tell you what you can do," added Colin, waving his hand. "You can tell Martha to bring them here. The boy is Martha's brother. His name is Dickon and he is an animal charmer."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I hope the animals won't bite, Master Colin," said the nurse.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I told you he was a charmer," said Colin austerely. "Charmers' animals never bite."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "There are snake-charmers in India," said Mary. "And they can put their snakes' heads in their mouths."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: They ate their breakfast with the morning air pouring in upon them. Colin's breakfast was a very good one and Mary watched him with serious interest.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "You will begin to get fatter just as I did," she said. "I never wanted my breakfast when I was in India and now I always want it."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I wanted mine this morning," said Colin. "Perhaps it was the fresh air. When do you think Dickon will come?"
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: He was not long in coming. In about ten minutes Mary held up her hand.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: Colin listened and heard it, the oddest sound in the world to hear inside a house, a hoarse "caw-caw."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "That's Soot," said Mary. "Listen again. Do you hear a bleat - a tiny one?"
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "That's the new-born lamb," said Mary. "He's coming."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: Dickon's moorland boots were thick and clumsy and though he tried to walk quietly they made a clumping sound as he walked through the long corridors. Mary and Colin heard him marching - marching, until he passed through the tapestry door on to the soft carpet of Colin's own passage.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "If you please, sir," announced Martha, opening the door, "if you please, sir, here's Dickon an' his creatures."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: Dickon came in smiling his nicest wide smile. The new-born lamb was in his arms and the little red fox trotted by his side. Nut sat on his left shoulder and Soot on his right and Shell's head and paws peeped out of his coat pocket.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: Colin slowly sat up and stared and stared - as he had stared when he first saw Mary; but this was a stare of wonder and delight. The truth was that in spite of all he had heard he had not in the least understood what this boy would be like and that his fox and his crow and his squirrels and his lamb were so near to him and his friendliness that they seemed almost to be part of himself. Colin had never talked to a boy in his life and he was so overwhelmed by his own pleasure and curiosity that he did not even think of speaking.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: But Dickon did not feel the least shy or awkward. He had not felt embarrassed because the crow had not known his language and had only stared and had not spoken to him the first time they met. Creatures were always like that until they found out about you. He walked over to Colin's sofa and put the new-born lamb quietly on his lap, and immediately the little creature turned to the warm velvet dressing-gown and began to nuzzle and nuzzle into its folds and butt its tight-curled head with soft impatience against his side. Of course no boy could have helped speaking then.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "What is it doing?" cried Colin. "What does it want?"
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "It wants its mother," said Dickon, smiling more and more. "I brought it to thee a bit hungry because I knowed tha'd like to see it feed."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: He knelt down by the sofa and took a feeding-bottle from his pocket.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Come on, little 'un," he said, turning the small woolly white head with a gentle brown hand. "This is what tha's after. Tha'll get more out o' this than tha' will out o' silk velvet coats. There now," and he pushed the rubber tip of the bottle into the nuzzling mouth and the lamb began to suck it with ravenous ecstasy.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: After that there was no wondering what to say. By the time the lamb fell asleep questions poured forth and Dickon answered them all. He told them how he had found the lamb just as the sun was rising three mornings ago. He had been standing on the moor listening to a skylark and watching him swing higher and higher into the sky until he was only a speck in the heights of blue.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I'd almost lost him but for his song an' I was wonderin' how a chap could hear it when it seemed as if he'd get out o' th' world in a minute - an' just then I heard somethin' else far off among th' gorse bushes. It was a weak bleatin' an' I knowed it was a new lamb as was hungry an' I knowed it wouldn't be hungry if it hadn't lost its mother somehow, so I set off searchin'. Eh! I did have a look for it. I went in an' out among th' gorse bushes an' round an' round an' I always seemed to take th' wrong turnin'. But at last I seed a bit o' white by a rock on top o' th' moor an' I climbed up an' found th' little 'un half dead wi' cold an' clemmin'."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: While he talked, Soot flew solemnly in and out of the open window and cawed remarks about the scenery while Nut and Shell made excursions into the big trees outside and ran up and down trunks and explored branches. Captain curled up near Dickon, who sat on the hearth-rug from preference.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: They looked at the pictures in the gardening books and Dickon knew all the flowers by their country names and knew exactly which ones were already growing in the secret garden.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I couldna' say that there name," he said, pointing to one under which was written "Aquilegia," "but us calls that a columbine, an' that there one it's a snapdragon and they both grow wild in hedges, but these is garden ones an' they're bigger an' grander. There's some big clumps o' columbine in th' garden. They'll look like a bed o' blue an' white butterflies flutterin' when they're out."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I'm going to see them," cried Colin. "I am going to see them!"
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Aye, that tha' mun," said Mary quite seriously. "An' tha' munnot lose no time about it."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: CHAPTER XX. "I SHALL LIVE FOREVER - AND EVER - AND EVER!"
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "They're same as us," said Dickon, "only they have to build their homes every year. An' it keeps 'em so busy they fair scuffle to get 'em done."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: Rumors of the new and curious things which were occurring in the invalid's apartments had of course filtered through the servants' hall into the stable yards and out among the gardeners, but notwithstanding this, Mr. Roach was startled one day when he received orders from Master Colin's room to the effect that he must report himself in the apartment no outsider had ever seen, as the invalid himself desired to speak to him.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Well, well," he said to himself as he hurriedly changed his coat, "what's to do now? His Royal Highness that wasn't to be looked at calling up a man he's never set eyes on."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: Mr. Roach was not without curiosity. He had never caught even a glimpse of the boy and had heard a dozen exaggerated stories about his uncanny looks and ways and his insane tempers. The thing he had heard oftenest was that he might die at any moment and there had been numerous fanciful descriptions of a humped back and helpless limbs, given by people who had never seen him.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Things are changing in this house, Mr. Roach," said Mrs. Medlock, as she led him up the back staircase to the corridor on to which opened the hitherto mysterious chamber.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Let's hope they're changing for the better, Mrs. Medlock," he answered.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "They couldn't well change for the worse," she continued; "and queer as it all is there's them as finds their duties made a lot easier to stand up under. Don't you be surprised, Mr. Roach, if you find yourself in the middle of a menagerie and Martha Sowerby's Dickon more at home than you or me could ever be."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: There really was a sort of Magic about Dickon, as Mary always privately believed. When Mr. Roach heard his name he smiled quite leniently.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "He'd be at home in Buckingham Palace or at the bottom of a coal mine," he said. "And yet it's not impudence, either. He's just fine, is that lad."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: It was perhaps well he had been prepared or he might have been startled. When the bedroom door was opened a large crow, which seemed quite at home perched on the high back of a carven chair, announced the entrance of a visitor by saying "Caw - Caw" quite loudly. In spite of Mrs. Medlock's warning, Mr. Roach only just escaped being sufficiently undignified to jump backward.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: The young Rajah was neither in bed nor on his sofa. He was sitting in an armchair and a young lamb was standing by him shaking its tail in feeding-lamb fashion as Dickon knelt giving it milk from its bottle. A squirrel was perched on Dickon's bent back attentively nibbling a nut. The little girl from India was sitting on a big footstool looking on.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Here is Mr. Roach, Master Colin," said Mrs. Medlock.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: The young Rajah turned and looked his servitor over - at least that was what the head gardener felt happened.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Oh, you are Roach, are you?" he said. "I sent for you to give you some very important orders."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Very good, sir," answered Roach, wondering if he was to receive instructions to fell all the oaks in the park or to transform the orchards into water-gardens.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I am going out in my chair this afternoon," said Colin. "If the fresh air agrees with me I may go out every day. When I go, none of the gardeners are to be anywhere near the Long Walk by the garden walls. No one is to be there. I shall go out about two o'clock and everyone must keep away until I send word that they may go back to their work."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Very good, sir," replied Mr. Roach, much relieved to hear that the oaks might remain and that the orchards were safe.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Mary," said Colin, turning to her, "what is that thing you say in India when you have finished talking and want people to go?"
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "You say, 'You have my permission to go,'" answered Mary.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "You have my permission to go, Roach," he said. "But, remember, this is very important."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Caw - Caw!" remarked the crow hoarsely but not impolitely.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Very good, sir. Thank you, sir," said Mr. Roach, and Mrs. Medlock took him out of the room.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: Outside in the corridor, being a rather good-natured man, he smiled until he almost laughed.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "My word!" he said, "he's got a fine lordly way with him, hasn't he? You'd think he was a whole Royal Family rolled into one - Prince Consort and all."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Eh!" protested Mrs. Medlock, "we've had to let him trample all over everyone of us ever since he had feet and he thinks that's what folks was born for."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Perhaps he'll grow out of it, if he lives," suggested Mr. Roach.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Well, there's one thing pretty sure," said Mrs. Medlock. "If he does live and that Indian child stays here I'll warrant she teaches him that the whole orange does not belong to him, as Susan Sowerby says. And he'll be likely to find out the size of his own quarter."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: Inside the room Colin was leaning back on his cushions.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "It's all safe now," he said. "And this afternoon I shall see it - this afternoon I shall be in it!"
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: Dickon went back to the garden with his creatures and Mary stayed with Colin. She did not think he looked tired but he was very quiet before their lunch came and he was quiet while they were eating it. She wondered why and asked him about it.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "What big eyes you've got, Colin," she said. "When you are thinking they get as big as saucers. What are you thinking about now?"
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I can't help thinking about what it will look like," he answered.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "The springtime," he said. "I was thinking that I've really never seen it before. I scarcely ever went out and when I did go I never looked at it. I didn't even think about it."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I never saw it in India because there wasn't any," said Mary.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: Shut in and morbid as his life had been, Colin had more imagination than she had and at least he had spent a good deal of time looking at wonderful books and pictures.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "That morning when you ran in and said 'It's come! It's come!', you made me feel quite queer. It sounded as if things were coming with a great procession and big bursts and wafts of music. I've a picture like it in one of my books - crowds of lovely people and children with garlands and branches with blossoms on them, everyone laughing and dancing and crowding and playing on pipes. That was why I said, 'Perhaps we shall hear golden trumpets' and told you to throw open the window."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "How funny!" said Mary. "That's really just what it feels like. And if all the flowers and leaves and green things and birds and wild creatures danced past at once, what a crowd it would be! I'm sure they'd dance and sing and flute and that would be the wafts of music."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: They both laughed but it was not because the idea was laughable but because they both so liked it.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: A little later the nurse made Colin ready. She noticed that instead of lying like a log while his clothes were put on he sat up and made some efforts to help himself, and he talked and laughed with Mary all the time.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "This is one of his good days, sir," she said to Dr. Craven, who dropped in to inspect him. "He's in such good spirits that it makes him stronger."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I'll call in again later in the afternoon, after he has come in," said Dr. Craven. "I must see how the going out agrees with him. I wish," in a very low voice, "that he would let you go with him."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I'd rather give up the case this moment, sir, than even stay here while it's suggested," answered the nurse. With sudden firmness.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I hadn't really decided to suggest it," said the doctor, with his slight nervousness. "We'll try the experiment. Dickon's a lad I'd trust with a new-born child."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: The strongest footman in the house carried Colin downstairs and put him in his wheeled chair near which Dickon waited outside. After the manservant had arranged his rugs and cushions the Rajah waved his hand to him and to the nurse.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "You have my permission to go," he said, and they both disappeared quickly and it must be confessed giggled when they were safely inside the house.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: Dickon began to push the wheeled chair slowly and steadily. Mistress Mary walked beside it and Colin leaned back and lifted his face to the sky. The arch of it looked very high and the small snowy clouds seemed like white birds floating on outspread wings below its crystal blueness. The wind swept in soft big breaths down from the moor and was strange with a wild clear scented sweetness. Colin kept lifting his thin chest to draw it in, and his big eyes looked as if it were they which were listening - listening, instead of his ears.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "There are so many sounds of singing and humming and calling out," he said. "What is that scent the puffs of wind bring?"
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "It's gorse on th' moor that's openin' out," answered Dickon. "Eh! th' bees are at it wonderful today."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: Not a human creature was to be caught sight of in the paths they took. In fact every gardener or gardener's lad had been witched away. But they wound in and out among the shrubbery and out and round the fountain beds, following their carefully planned route for the mere mysterious pleasure of it. But when at last they turned into the Long Walk by the ivied walls the excited sense of an approaching thrill made them, for some curious reason they could not have explained, begin to speak in whispers.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "This is it," breathed Mary. "This is where I used to walk up and down and wonder and wonder."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Is it?" cried Colin, and his eyes began to search the ivy with eager curiousness. "But I can see nothing," he whispered. "There is no door."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: Then there was a lovely breathless silence and the chair wheeled on.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "That is the garden where Ben Weatherstaff works," said Mary.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "This is where the robin flew over the wall," she said.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Is it?" cried Colin. "Oh! I wish he'd come again!"
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "And that," said Mary with solemn delight, pointing under a big lilac bush, "is where he perched on the little heap of earth and showed me the key."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Where? Where? There?" he cried, and his eyes were as big as the wolf's in Red Riding-Hood, when Red Riding-Hood felt called upon to remark on them. Dickon stood still and the wheeled chair stopped.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "And this," said Mary, stepping on to the bed close to the ivy, "is where I went to talk to him when he chirped at me from the top of the wall. And this is the ivy the wind blew back," and she took hold of the hanging green curtain.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "And here is the handle, and here is the door. Dickon push him in - push him in quickly!"
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: And Dickon did it with one strong, steady, splendid push.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I shall get well! I shall get well!" he cried out. "Mary! Dickon! I shall get well! And I shall live forever and ever and ever!"
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: And it was like that with Colin when he first saw and heard and felt the Springtime inside the four high walls of a hidden garden. That afternoon the whole world seemed to devote itself to being perfect and radiantly beautiful and kind to one boy. Perhaps out of pure heavenly goodness the spring came and crowded everything it possibly could into that one place. More than once Dickon paused in what he was doing and stood still with a sort of growing wonder in his eyes, shaking his head softly.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Eh! it is graidely," he said. "I'm twelve goin' on thirteen an' there's a lot o' afternoons in thirteen years, but seems to me like I never seed one as graidely as this 'ere."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Aye, it is a graidely one," said Mary, and she sighed for mere joy. "I'll warrant it's the graidelest one as ever was in this world."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Does tha' think," said Colin with dreamy carefulness, "as happen it was made loike this 'ere all o' purpose for me?"
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "My word!" cried Mary admiringly, "that there is a bit o' good Yorkshire. Tha'rt shapin' first-rate - that tha' art."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: They drew the chair under the plum-tree, which was snow-white with blossoms and musical with bees. It was like a king's canopy, a fairy king's. There were flowering cherry-trees near and apple-trees whose buds were pink and white, and here and there one had burst open wide. Between the blossoming branches of the canopy bits of blue sky looked down like wonderful eyes.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: Mary and Dickon worked a little here and there and Colin watched them. They brought him things to look at - buds which were opening, buds which were tight closed, bits of twig whose leaves were just showing green, the feather of a woodpecker which had dropped on the grass, the empty shell of some bird early hatched. Dickon pushed the chair slowly round and round the garden, stopping every other moment to let him look at wonders springing out of the earth or trailing down from trees. It was like being taken in state round the country of a magic king and queen and shown all the mysterious riches it contained.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I wonder if we shall see the robin?" said Colin.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Tha'll see him often enow after a bit," answered Dickon. "When th' eggs hatches out th' little chap he'll be kep' so busy it'll make his head swim. Tha'll see him flyin' backward an' for'ard carryin' worms nigh as big as himsel' an' that much noise goin' on in th' nest when he gets there as fair flusters him so as he scarce knows which big mouth to drop th' first piece in. An' gapin' beaks an' squawks on every side. Mother says as when she sees th' work a robin has to keep them gapin' beaks filled, she feels like she was a lady with nothin' to do. She says she's seen th' little chaps when it seemed like th' sweat must be droppin' off 'em, though folk can't see it."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: This made them giggle so delightedly that they were obliged to cover their mouths with their hands, remembering that they must not be heard. Colin had been instructed as to the law of whispers and low voices several days before. He liked the mysteriousness of it and did his best, but in the midst of excited enjoyment it is rather difficult never to laugh above a whisper.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: Every moment of the afternoon was full of new things and every hour the sunshine grew more golden. The wheeled chair had been drawn back under the canopy and Dickon had sat down on the grass and had just drawn out his pipe when Colin saw something he had not had time to notice before.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "That's a very old tree over there, isn't it?" he said.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: Dickon looked across the grass at the tree and Mary looked and there was a brief moment of stillness.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Yes," answered Dickon, after it, and his low voice had a very gentle sound.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "The branches are quite gray and there's not a single leaf anywhere," Colin went on. "It's quite dead, isn't it?"
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Aye," admitted Dickon. "But them roses as has climbed all over it will near hide every bit o' th' dead wood when they're full o' leaves an' flowers. It won't look dead then. It'll be th' prettiest of all."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "It looks as if a big branch had been broken off," said Colin. "I wonder how it was done."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "It's been done many a year," answered Dickon. "Eh!" with a sudden relieved start and laying his hand on Colin. "Look at that robin! There he is! He's been foragin' for his mate."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: Colin was almost too late but he just caught sight of him, the flash of red-breasted bird with something in his beak. He darted through the greenness and into the close-grown corner and was out of sight. Colin leaned back on his cushion again, laughing a little.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "He's taking her tea to her. Perhaps it's five o'clock. I think I'd like some tea myself."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "It was Magic which sent the robin," said Mary secretly to Dickon afterward. "I know it was Magic." For both she and Dickon had been afraid Colin might ask something about the tree whose branch had broken off ten years ago and they had talked it over together and Dickon had stood and rubbed his head in a troubled way.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "We mun look as if it wasn't no different from th' other trees," he had said. "We couldn't never tell him how it broke, poor lad. If he says anything about it we mun - we mun try to look cheerful."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: But she had not felt as if she looked cheerful when she gazed at the tree. She wondered and wondered in those few moments if there was any reality in that other thing Dickon had said. He had gone on rubbing his rust-red hair in a puzzled way, but a nice comforted look had begun to grow in his blue eyes.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Mrs. Craven was a very lovely young lady," he had gone on rather hesitatingly. "An' mother she thinks maybe she's about Misselthwaite many a time lookin' after Mester Colin, same as all mothers do when they're took out o' th' world. They have to come back, tha' sees. Happen she's been in the garden an' happen it was her set us to work, an' told us to bring him here."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: They saw the robin carry food to his mate two or three times, and it was so suggestive of afternoon tea that Colin felt they must have some.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Go and make one of the men servants bring some in a basket to the rhododendron walk," he said. "And then you and Dickon can bring it here."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: It was an agreeable idea, easily carried out, and when the white cloth was spread upon the grass, with hot tea and buttered toast and crumpets, a delightfully hungry meal was eaten, and several birds on domestic errands paused to inquire what was going on and were led into investigating crumbs with great activity. Nut and Shell whisked up trees with pieces of cake and Soot took the entire half of a buttered crumpet into a corner and pecked at and examined and turned it over and made hoarse remarks about it until he decided to swallow it all joyfully in one gulp.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: The afternoon was dragging towards its mellow hour. The sun was deepening the gold of its lances, the bees were going home and the birds were flying past less often. Dickon and Mary were sitting on the grass, the tea-basket was repacked ready to be taken back to the house, and Colin was lying against his cushions with his heavy locks pushed back from his forehead and his face looking quite a natural color.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I don't want this afternoon to go," he said; "but I shall come back tomorrow, and the day after, and the day after, and the day after."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "You'll get plenty of fresh air, won't you?" said Mary.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I'm going to get nothing else," he answered. "I've seen the spring now and I'm going to see the summer. I'm going to see everything grow here. I'm going to grow here myself."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "That tha' will," said Dickon. "Us'll have thee walkin' about here an' diggin' same as other folk afore long."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: Dickon's glance at him was delicately cautious. Neither he nor Mary had ever asked if anything was the matter with his legs.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "For sure tha' will," he said stoutly. "Tha - tha's got legs o' thine own, same as other folks!"
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: Mary was rather frightened until she heard Colin's answer.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Nothing really ails them," he said, "but they are so thin and weak. They shake so that I'm afraid to try to stand on them."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "When tha' stops bein' afraid tha'lt stand on 'em," Dickon said with renewed cheer. "An' tha'lt stop bein' afraid in a bit."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I shall?" said Colin, and he lay still as if he were wondering about things.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: They were really very quiet for a little while. The sun was dropping lower. It was that hour when everything stills itself, and they really had had a busy and exciting afternoon. Colin looked as if he were resting luxuriously. Even the creatures had ceased moving about and had drawn together and were resting near them. Soot had perched on a low branch and drawn up one leg and dropped the gray film drowsily over his eyes. Mary privately thought he looked as if he might snore in a minute.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: Mary and Dickon wheeled about and looked. There was Ben Weatherstaff's indignant face glaring at them over the wall from the top of a ladder! He actually shook his fist at Mary.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "If I wasn't a bachelder, an' tha' was a wench o' mine," he cried, "I'd give thee a hidin'!"
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: He mounted another step threateningly as if it were his energetic intention to jump down and deal with her; but as she came toward him he evidently thought better of it and stood on the top step of his ladder shaking his fist down at her.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Ben Weatherstaff," called out Mary, finding her breath. She stood below him and called up to him with a sort of gasp. "Ben Weatherstaff, it was the robin who showed me the way!"
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: Then it did seem as if Ben really would scramble down on her side of the wall, he was so outraged.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Tha' young bad 'un!" he called down at her. "Layin' tha' badness on a robin - not but what he's impidint enow for anythin'. Him showin' thee th' way! Him! Eh! tha' young nowt" - she could see his next words burst out because he was overpowered by curiosity - "however i' this world did tha' get in?"
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "It was the robin who showed me the way," she protested obstinately. "He didn't know he was doing it but he did. And I can't tell you from here while you're shaking your fist at me."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: He stopped shaking his fist very suddenly at that very moment and his jaw actually dropped as he stared over her head at something he saw coming over the grass toward him.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: At the first sound of his torrent of words Colin had been so surprised that he had only sat up and listened as if he were spellbound. But in the midst of it he had recovered himself and beckoned imperiously to Dickon.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Wheel me over there!" he commanded. "Wheel me quite close and stop right in front of him!"
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: And this, if you please, this is what Ben Weatherstaff beheld and which made his jaw drop. A wheeled chair with luxurious cushions and robes which came toward him looking rather like some sort of State Coach because a young Rajah leaned back in it with royal command in his great black-rimmed eyes and a thin white hand extended haughtily toward him. And it stopped right under Ben Weatherstaff's nose. It was really no wonder his mouth dropped open.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: How Ben Weatherstaff stared! His red old eyes fixed themselves on what was before him as if he were seeing a ghost. He gazed and gazed and gulped a lump down his throat and did not say a word.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Do you know who I am?" demanded Colin still more imperiously. "Answer!"
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: Ben Weatherstaff put his gnarled hand up and passed it over his eyes and over his forehead and then he did answer in a queer shaky voice.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Who tha' art?" he said. "Aye, that I do - wi' tha' mother's eyes starin' at me out o' tha' face. Lord knows how tha' come here. But tha'rt th' poor cripple."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: Colin forgot that he had ever had a back. His face flushed scarlet and he sat bolt upright.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I'm not a cripple!" he cried out furiously. "I'm not!"
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "He's not!" cried Mary, almost shouting up the wall in her fierce indignation. "He's not got a lump as big as a pin! I looked and there was none there - not one!"
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: Ben Weatherstaff passed his hand over his forehead again and gazed as if he could never gaze enough. His hand shook and his mouth shook and his voice shook. He was an ignorant old man and a tactless old man and he could only remember the things he had heard.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Tha' - tha' hasn't got a crooked back?" he said hoarsely.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Tha' - tha' hasn't got crooked legs?" quavered Ben more hoarsely yet.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: It was too much. The strength which Colin usually threw into his tantrums rushed through him now in a new way. Never yet had he been accused of crooked legs - even in whispers - and the perfectly simple belief in their existence which was revealed by Ben Weatherstaff's voice was more than Rajah flesh and blood could endure. His anger and insulted pride made him forget everything but this one moment and filled him with a power he had never known before, an almost unnatural strength.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Come here!" he shouted to Dickon, and he actually began to tear the coverings off his lower limbs and disentangle himself. "Come here! Come here! This minute!"
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: Dickon was by his side in a second. Mary caught her breath in a short gasp and felt herself turn pale.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "He can do it! He can do it! He can do it! He can!" she gabbled over to herself under her breath as fast as ever she could.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: There was a brief fierce scramble, the rugs were tossed on the ground, Dickon held Colin's arm, the thin legs were out, the thin feet were on the grass. Colin was standing upright - upright - as straight as an arrow and looking strangely tall - his head thrown back and his strange eyes flashing lightning.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Look at me!" he flung up at Ben Weatherstaff. "Just look at me - you! Just look at me!"
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "He's as straight as I am!" cried Dickon. "He's as straight as any lad i' Yorkshire!"
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: What Ben Weatherstaff did Mary thought queer beyond measure. He choked and gulped and suddenly tears ran down his weather-wrinkled cheeks as he struck his old hands together.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Eh!" he burst forth, "th' lies folk tells! Tha'rt as thin as a lath an' as white as a wraith, but there's not a knob on thee. Tha'lt make a mon yet. God bless thee!"
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: Dickon held Colin's arm strongly but the boy had not begun to falter. He stood straighter and straighter and looked Ben Weatherstaff in the face.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I'm your master," he said, "when my father is away. And you are to obey me. This is my garden. Don't dare to say a word about it! You get down from that ladder and go out to the Long Walk and Miss Mary will meet you and bring you here. I want to talk to you. We did not want you, but now you will have to be in the secret. Be quick!"
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: Ben Weatherstaff's crabbed old face was still wet with that one queer rush of tears. It seemed as if he could not take his eyes from thin straight Colin standing on his feet with his head thrown back.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Eh! lad," he almost whispered. "Eh! my lad!" And then remembering himself he suddenly touched his hat gardener fashion and said, "Yes, sir! Yes, sir!" and obediently disappeared as he descended the ladder.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: When his head was out of sight Colin turned to Mary.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Go and meet him," he said; and Mary flew across the grass to the door under the ivy.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: Dickon was watching him with sharp eyes. There were scarlet spots on his cheeks and he looked amazing, but he showed no signs of falling.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I can stand," he said, and his head was still held up and he said it quite grandly.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I told thee tha' could as soon as tha' stopped bein' afraid," answered Dickon. "An' tha's stopped."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: Then suddenly he remembered something Mary had said.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: Dickon's curly mouth spread in a cheerful grin.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Tha's doin' Magic thysel'," he said. "It's same Magic as made these 'ere work out o' th' earth," and he touched with his thick boot a clump of crocuses in the grass.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Aye," he said slowly, "there couldna' be bigger Magic than that there - there couldna' be."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I'm going to walk to that tree," he said, pointing to one a few feet away from him. "I'm going to be standing when Weatherstaff comes here. I can rest against the tree if I like. When I want to sit down I will sit down, but not before. Bring a rug from the chair."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: He walked to the tree and though Dickon held his arm he was wonderfully steady. When he stood against the tree trunk it was not too plain that he supported himself against it, and he still held himself so straight that he looked tall.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: When Ben Weatherstaff came through the door in the wall he saw him standing there and he heard Mary muttering something under her breath.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "What art sayin'?" he asked rather testily because he did not want his attention distracted from the long thin straight boy figure and proud face.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "You can do it! You can do it! I told you you could! You can do it! You can do it! You can!"
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: She was saying it to Colin because she wanted to make Magic and keep him on his feet looking like that. She could not bear that he should give in before Ben Weatherstaff. He did not give in. She was uplifted by a sudden feeling that he looked quite beautiful in spite of his thinness. He fixed his eyes on Ben Weatherstaff in his funny imperious way.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Look at me!" he commanded. "Look at me all over! Am I a hunchback? Have I got crooked legs?"
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: Ben Weatherstaff had not quite got over his emotion, but he had recovered a little and answered almost in his usual way.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Not tha'," he said. "Nowt o' th' sort. What's tha' been doin' with thysel' - hidin' out o' sight an' lettin' folk think tha' was cripple an' half-witted?"
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Half-witted!" said Colin angrily. "Who thought that?"
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Lots o' fools," said Ben. "Th' world's full o' jackasses brayin' an' they never bray nowt but lies. What did tha' shut thysel' up for?"
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Everyone thought I was going to die," said Colin shortly. "I'm not!"
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: And he said it with such decision Ben Weatherstaff looked him over, up and down, down and up.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Tha' die!" he said with dry exultation. "Nowt o' th' sort! Tha's got too much pluck in thee. When I seed thee put tha' legs on th' ground in such a hurry I knowed tha' was all right. Sit thee down on th' rug a bit young Mester an' give me thy orders."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: There was a queer mixture of crabbed tenderness and shrewd understanding in his manner. Mary had poured out speech as rapidly as she could as they had come down the Long Walk. The chief thing to be remembered, she had told him, was that Colin was getting well - getting well. The garden was doing it. No one must let him remember about having humps and dying.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: The Rajah condescended to seat himself on a rug under the tree.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "What work do you do in the gardens, Weatherstaff?" he inquired.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Anythin' I'm told to do," answered old Ben. "I'm kep' on by favor - because she liked me."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "My mother?" said Colin, and he looked about him quietly. "This was her garden, wasn't it?"
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Aye, it was that!" and Ben Weatherstaff looked about him too. "She were main fond of it."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "It is my garden now. I am fond of it. I shall come here every day," announced Colin. "But it is to be a secret. My orders are that no one is to know that we come here. Dickon and my cousin have worked and made it come alive. I shall send for you sometimes to help - but you must come when no one can see you."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: Ben Weatherstaff's face twisted itself in a dry old smile.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I've come here before when no one saw me," he said.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Th' last time I was here," rubbing his chin and looking round, "was about two year' ago."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "But no one has been in it for ten years!" cried Colin.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I'm no one," said old Ben dryly. "An' I didn't come through th' door. I come over th' wall. Th' rheumatics held me back th' last two year'."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Tha' come an' did a bit o' prunin'!" cried Dickon. "I couldn't make out how it had been done."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "She was so fond of it - she was!" said Ben Weatherstaff slowly. "An' she was such a pretty young thing. She says to me once, 'Ben,' says she laughin', 'if ever I'm ill or if I go away you must take care of my roses.' When she did go away th' orders was no one was ever to come nigh. But I come," with grumpy obstinacy. "Over th' wall I come - until th' rheumatics stopped me - an' I did a bit o' work once a year. She'd gave her order first."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "It wouldn't have been as wick as it is if tha' hadn't done it," said Dickon. "I did wonder."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I'm glad you did it, Weatherstaff," said Colin. "You'll know how to keep the secret."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Aye, I'll know, sir," answered Ben. "An' it'll be easier for a man wi' rheumatics to come in at th' door."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: On the grass near the tree Mary had dropped her trowel. Colin stretched out his hand and took it up. An odd expression came into his face and he began to scratch at the earth. His thin hand was weak enough but presently as they watched him - Mary with quite breathless interest - he drove the end of the trowel into the soil and turned some over.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "You can do it! You can do it!" said Mary to herself. "I tell you, you can!"
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: Dickon's round eyes were full of eager curiousness but he said not a word. Ben Weatherstaff looked on with interested face.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: Colin persevered. After he had turned a few trowelfuls of soil he spoke exultantly to Dickon in his best Yorkshire.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Tha' said as tha'd have me walkin' about here same as other folk - an' tha' said tha'd have me diggin'. I thowt tha' was just leein' to please me. This is only th' first day an' I've walked - an' here I am diggin'."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: Ben Weatherstaff's mouth fell open again when he heard him, but he ended by chuckling.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Eh!" he said, "that sounds as if tha'd got wits enow. Tha'rt a Yorkshire lad for sure. An' tha'rt diggin', too. How'd tha' like to plant a bit o' somethin'? I can get thee a rose in a pot."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Go and get it!" said Colin, digging excitedly. "Quick! Quick!"
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: It was done quickly enough indeed. Ben Weatherstaff went his way forgetting rheumatics. Dickon took his spade and dug the hole deeper and wider than a new digger with thin white hands could make it. Mary slipped out to run and bring back a watering-can. When Dickon had deepened the hole Colin went on turning the soft earth over and over. He looked up at the sky, flushed and glowing with the strangely new exercise, slight as it was.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I want to do it before the sun goes quite - quite down," he said.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: Mary thought that perhaps the sun held back a few minutes just on purpose. Ben Weatherstaff brought the rose in its pot from the greenhouse. He hobbled over the grass as fast as he could. He had begun to be excited, too. He knelt down by the hole and broke the pot from the mould.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Here, lad," he said, handing the plant to Colin. "Set it in the earth thysel' same as th' king does when he goes to a new place."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: The thin white hands shook a little and Colin's flush grew deeper as he set the rose in the mould and held it while old Ben made firm the earth. It was filled in and pressed down and made steady. Mary was leaning forward on her hands and knees. Soot had flown down and marched forward to see what was being done. Nut and Shell chattered about it from a cherry-tree.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "It's planted!" said Colin at last. "And the sun is only slipping over the edge. Help me up, Dickon. I want to be standing when it goes. That's part of the Magic."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: And Dickon helped him, and the Magic - or whatever it was - so gave him strength that when the sun did slip over the edge and end the strange lovely afternoon for them there he actually stood on his two feet - laughing.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: Dr. Craven had been waiting some time at the house when they returned to it. He had indeed begun to wonder if it might not be wise to send someone out to explore the garden paths. When Colin was brought back to his room the poor man looked him over seriously.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "You should not have stayed so long," he said. "You must not overexert yourself."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I am not tired at all," said Colin. "It has made me well. Tomorrow I am going out in the morning as well as in the afternoon."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I am not sure that I can allow it," answered Dr. Craven. "I am afraid it would not be wise."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "It would not be wise to try to stop me," said Colin quite seriously. "I am going."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I'm thinking that I am rather sorry for Dr. Craven."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "So am I," said Colin calmly, but not without an air of some satisfaction. "He won't get Misselthwaite at all now I'm not going to die."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I'm sorry for him because of that, of course," said Mary, "but I was thinking just then that it must have been very horrid to have had to be polite for ten years to a boy who was always rude. I would never have done it."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "If you had been his own boy and he had been a slapping sort of man," said Mary, "he would have slapped you."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "No, he daren't," answered Mistress Mary, thinking the thing out quite without prejudice. "Nobody ever dared to do anything you didn't like - because you were going to die and things like that. You were such a poor thing."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "But," announced Colin stubbornly, "I am not going to be a poor thing. I won't let people think I'm one. I stood on my feet this afternoon."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "It is always having your own way that has made you so queer," Mary went on, thinking aloud.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Yes," answered Mary, "very. But you needn't be cross," she added impartially, "because so am I queer - and so is Ben Weatherstaff. But I am not as queer as I was before I began to like people and before I found the garden."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I don't want to be queer," said Colin. "I am not going to be," and he frowned again with determination.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: He was a very proud boy. He lay thinking for a while and then Mary saw his beautiful smile begin and gradually change his whole face.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I shall stop being queer," he said, "if I go every day to the garden. There is Magic in there - good Magic, you know, Mary. I am sure there is."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Even if it isn't real Magic," Colin said, "we can pretend it is. Something is there - something!"
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "It's Magic," said Mary, "but not black. It's as white as snow."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "She was main fond o' them - she was," Ben Weatherstaff said. "She liked them things as was allus pointin' up to th' blue sky, she used to tell. Not as she was one o' them as looked down on th' earth - not her. She just loved it but she said as th' blue sky allus looked so joyful."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: And this was not the half of the Magic. The fact that he had really once stood on his feet had set Colin thinking tremendously and when Mary told him of the spell she had worked he was excited and approved of it greatly. He talked of it constantly.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Of course there must be lots of Magic in the world," he said wisely one day, "but people don't know what it is like or how to make it. Perhaps the beginning is just to say nice things are going to happen until you make them happen. I am going to try and experiment."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: The next morning when they went to the secret garden he sent at once for Ben Weatherstaff. Ben came as quickly as he could and found the Rajah standing on his feet under a tree and looking very grand but also very beautifully smiling.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Good morning, Ben Weatherstaff," he said. "I want you and Dickon and Miss Mary to stand in a row and listen to me because I am going to tell you something very important."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I am going to try a scientific experiment," explained the Rajah. "When I grow up I am going to make great scientific discoveries and I am going to begin now with this experiment."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Aye, aye, sir!" said Ben Weatherstaff promptly, though this was the first time he had heard of great scientific discoveries.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: It was the first time Mary had heard of them, either, but even at this stage she had begun to realize that, queer as he was, Colin had read about a great many singular things and was somehow a very convincing sort of boy. When he held up his head and fixed his strange eyes on you it seemed as if you believed him almost in spite of yourself though he was only ten years old - going on eleven. At this moment he was especially convincing because he suddenly felt the fascination of actually making a sort of speech like a grown-up person.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "The great scientific discoveries I am going to make," he went on, "will be about Magic. Magic is a great thing and scarcely anyone knows anything about it except a few people in old books - and Mary a little, because she was born in India where there are fakirs. I believe Dickon knows some Magic, but perhaps he doesn't know he knows it. He charms animals and people. I would never have let him come to see me if he had not been an animal charmer - which is a boy charmer, too, because a boy is an animal. I am sure there is Magic in everything, only we have not sense enough to get hold of it and make it do things for us - like electricity and horses and steam."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: This sounded so imposing that Ben Weatherstaff became quite excited and really could not keep still.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Aye, aye, sir," he said and he began to stand up quite straight.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Aye, aye, sir!" said Ben Weatherstaff. "Aye, aye!"
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "If you keep doing it every day as regularly as soldiers go through drill we shall see what will happen and find out if the experiment succeeds. You learn things by saying them over and over and thinking about them until they stay in your mind forever and I think it will be the same with Magic. If you keep calling it to come to you and help you it will get to be part of you and it will stay and do things."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I once heard an officer in India tell my mother that there were fakirs who said words over and over thousands of times," said Mary.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I've heard Jem Fettleworth's wife say th' same thing over thousands o' times - callin' Jem a drunken brute," said Ben Weatherstaff dryly. "Summat allus come o' that, sure enough. He gave her a good hidin' an' went to th' Blue Lion an' got as drunk as a lord."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: Colin drew his brows together and thought a few minutes. Then he cheered up.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Well," he said, "you see something did come of it. She used the wrong Magic until she made him beat her. If she'd used the right Magic and had said something nice perhaps he wouldn't have got as drunk as a lord and perhaps - perhaps he might have bought her a new bonnet."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: Ben Weatherstaff chuckled and there was shrewd admiration in his little old eyes.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Tha'rt a clever lad as well as a straight-legged one, Mester Colin," he said. "Next time I see Bess Fettleworth I'll give her a bit of a hint o' what Magic will do for her. She'd be rare an' pleased if th' sinetifik 'speriment worked - an' so 'ud Jem."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: Dickon had stood listening to the lecture, his round eyes shining with curious delight. Nut and Shell were on his shoulders and he held a long-eared white rabbit in his arm and stroked and stroked it softly while it laid its ears along its back and enjoyed itself.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Do you think the experiment will work?" Colin asked him, wondering what he was thinking. He so often wondered what Dickon was thinking when he saw him looking at him or at one of his "creatures" with his happy wide smile.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: He smiled now and his smile was wider than usual.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Aye," he answered, "that I do. It'll work same as th' seeds do when th' sun shines on 'em. It'll work for sure. Shall us begin it now?"
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "It will be like sitting in a sort of temple," said Colin. "I'm rather tired and I want to sit down."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Eh!" said Dickon, "tha' mustn't begin by sayin' tha'rt tired. Tha' might spoil th' Magic."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: Colin turned and looked at him - into his innocent round eyes.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "That's true," he said slowly. "I must only think of the Magic."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "The 'creatures' have come," said Colin gravely. "They want to help us."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: Colin really looked quite beautiful, Mary thought. He held his head high as if he felt like a sort of priest and his strange eyes had a wonderful look in them. The light shone on him through the tree canopy.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Now we will begin," he said. "Shall we sway backward and forward, Mary, as if we were dervishes?"
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I canna' do no swayin' back'ard and for'ard," said Ben Weatherstaff. "I've got th' rheumatics."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "The Magic will take them away," said Colin in a High Priest tone, "but we won't sway until it has done it. We will only chant."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I canna' do no chantin'" said Ben Weatherstaff a trifle testily. "They turned me out o' th' church choir th' only time I ever tried it."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: No one smiled. They were all too much in earnest. Colin's face was not even crossed by a shadow. He was thinking only of the Magic.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Then I will chant," he said. And he began, looking like a strange boy spirit. "The sun is shining - the sun is shining. That is the Magic. The flowers are growing - the roots are stirring. That is the Magic. Being alive is the Magic - being strong is the Magic. The Magic is in me - the Magic is in me. It is in me - it is in me. It's in everyone of us. It's in Ben Weatherstaff's back. Magic! Magic! Come and help!"
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: He said it a great many times - not a thousand times but quite a goodly number. Mary listened entranced. She felt as if it were at once queer and beautiful and she wanted him to go on and on. Ben Weatherstaff began to feel soothed into a sort of dream which was quite agreeable. The humming of the bees in the blossoms mingled with the chanting voice and drowsily melted into a doze. Dickon sat cross-legged with his rabbit asleep on his arm and a hand resting on the lamb's back. Soot had pushed away a squirrel and huddled close to him on his shoulder, the gray film dropped over his eyes. At last Colin stopped.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Now I am going to walk round the garden," he announced.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: Ben Weatherstaff's head had just dropped forward and he lifted it with a jerk.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Nowt o' th' sort," mumbled Ben. "Th' sermon was good enow - but I'm bound to get out afore th' collection."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Not me," said Ben, straightening himself. "Who said I were? I heard every bit of it. You said th' Magic was in my back. Th' doctor calls it rheumatics."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "That was the wrong Magic," he said. "You will get better. You have my permission to go to your work. But come back tomorrow."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I'd like to see thee walk round the garden," grunted Ben.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: It was not an unfriendly grunt, but it was a grunt. In fact, being a stubborn old party and not having entire faith in Magic he had made up his mind that if he were sent away he would climb his ladder and look over the wall so that he might be ready to hobble back if there were any stumbling.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: The Rajah did not object to his staying and so the procession was formed. It really did look like a procession. Colin was at its head with Dickon on one side and Mary on the other. Ben Weatherstaff walked behind, and the "creatures" trailed after them, the lamb and the fox cub keeping close to Dickon, the white rabbit hopping along or stopping to nibble and Soot following with the solemnity of a person who felt himself in charge.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: It was a procession which moved slowly but with dignity. Every few yards it stopped to rest. Colin leaned on Dickon's arm and privately Ben Weatherstaff kept a sharp lookout, but now and then Colin took his hand from its support and walked a few steps alone. His head was held up all the time and he looked very grand.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "The Magic is in me!" he kept saying. "The Magic is making me strong! I can feel it! I can feel it!"
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: It seemed very certain that something was upholding and uplifting him. He sat on the seats in the alcoves, and once or twice he sat down on the grass and several times he paused in the path and leaned on Dickon, but he would not give up until he had gone all round the garden. When he returned to the canopy tree his cheeks were flushed and he looked triumphant.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "I did it! The Magic worked!" he cried. "That is my first scientific discovery."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "He will think he is in a dream," cried Mary. "He won't believe his eyes."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: Colin flushed triumphantly. He had made himself believe that he was going to get well, which was really more than half the battle, if he had been aware of it. And the thought which stimulated him more than any other was this imagining what his father would look like when he saw that he had a son who was as straight and strong as other fathers' sons. One of his darkest miseries in the unhealthy morbid past days had been his hatred of being a sickly weak-backed boy whose father was afraid to look at him.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "One of the things I am going to do, after the Magic works and before I begin to make scientific discoveries, is to be an athlete."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "We shall have thee takin' to boxin' in a week or so," said Ben Weatherstaff. "Tha'lt end wi' winnin' th' Belt an' bein' champion prize-fighter of all England."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Weatherstaff," he said, "that is disrespectful. You must not take liberties because you are in the secret. However much the Magic works I shall not be a prize-fighter. I shall be a Scientific Discoverer."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "Ax pardon - ax pardon, sir" answered Ben, touching his forehead in salute. "I ought to have seed it wasn't a jokin' matter," but his eyes twinkled and secretly he was immensely pleased. He really did not mind being snubbed since the snubbing meant that the lad was gaining strength and spirit.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: The secret garden was not the only one Dickon worked in. Round the cottage on the moor there was a piece of ground enclosed by a low wall of rough stones. Early in the morning and late in the fading twilight and on all the days Colin and Mary did not see him, Dickon worked there planting or tending potatoes and cabbages, turnips and carrots and herbs for his mother. In the company of his "creatures" he did wonders there and was never tired of doing them, it seemed. While he dug or weeded he whistled or sang bits of Yorkshire moor songs or talked to Soot or Captain or the brothers and sisters he had taught to help him.
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "We'd never get on as comfortable as we do," Mrs. Sowerby said, "if it wasn't for Dickon's garden. Anything'll grow for him. His 'taters and cabbages is twice th' size of anyone else's an' they've got a flavor with 'em as nobody's has."
quotes.source: The Secret Garden — Frances Hodgson Burnett

quotes.text: "All a chap's got to do to make 'em thrive, mother," he would say, "is to be friends with 'em for sure. They're just like th' 'creatures.'
